505537|2026-06.headline: Zee Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR 789 million (4.1% margin) as advertising dropped 11% YoY, while ZEE5 revenue rose 58% to INR 4,571 million.
505537|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was weighed down by an 11% YoY decline in advertising revenue, attributed to the Middle East conflict hitting April and May, and by a 15% rise in operating costs from FIFA 2026 marketing and new sports channel launches. Subscription revenue grew 16% YoY, and ZEE5 revenue grew 58% YoY to INR 4,571 million, though the digital business posted only INR 44 million EBITDA. Linear network share reached 20% (17.9% for the quarter through week 24), and PAT was INR 743 million. Management said significant FIFA revenue and cost will flow through in Q2, and it declined to give full-year EBITDA margin guidance.

segments.name: Digital (ZEE5)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 58% YoY to INR 4,571 million, with profitable growth for the third consecutive quarter, but EBITDA only INR 44 million after higher FIFA and Bullet marketing spend. 38 shows and movies released in the quarter, including 15 originals, across 7 languages.

segments.name: Linear broadcast
segments.commentary: All-time high network share of around 20%; quarterly share of 17.9%, up 110 bps YoY (data only through week 24 as BARC stopped publishing). Zee TV led prime time for 32+ consecutive weeks; Zee Cinema led movie genre at 27% viewership in week 22.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Declined 11% YoY on Middle East conflict in April and May; June saw green shoots after FIFA rights, with advertisers engaging on premium sponsorships.

segments.name: Music
segments.commentary: 54 billion total video views and over 177 million YouTube subscribers; catalogue of over 20,000 songs. Management described profitability as healthy.

segments.name: Studios (other sales and services)
segments.commentary: Other sales and services up 17% YoY; studios released 9 movies (4 Hindi, 5 other languages).

segments.name: Sports
segments.commentary: Secured FIFA digital and broadcast rights until 2034 (39 events, 38 still to go), plus Bundesliga and Serie A. Four Unite8 sports channels launched in June 2026. FIFA reach exceeded 400 million, with around 83% of FIFA viewership live on ZEE5.

guidance_outlook: No full-year EBITDA margin guidance given, citing market uncertainty.
Significant portion of FIFA revenue and cost expected in Q2 FY27 versus Q1; subscription revenue on accrual basis to see significant boost in Q2.
Digital growth momentum expected to continue in Q2 as FIFA gains accrue.
Management cautiously optimistic on advertising, citing market share gains, festive season and easing West Asia conflict.
Linear subscription price hikes to be considered at next NTO cycle, expected around February 2027.
capex_capacity: Unite8 sports channels (4) launched June 2026.
Heavy past capex at technology centre flowing through amortisation; management said current D&A run rate is within a reasonable range and not expected to significantly affect results.
Inventory increase largely due to FIFA rights outflows in Q1, which will flow through P&L in Q2.
demand_pricing: Advertising weak in April-May; June improved with FIFA sponsorships. Management views ad recovery as dependent on festive season, market share gains and West Asia de-escalation.
ZEE5 renewals said to be holding up beyond FIFA; language packs aiding subscription growth (no numbers disclosed).
B2C subscribers more than doubled in the quarter, partly FIFA-driven; B2B deals under discussion but not disclosed.
Sports rights costs are high versus regular content; management stressed selective buying and audience-led value.

qa_highlights.question: When will sports turn sustainably profitable, and will premium advertisers stay post-FIFA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sports will be run prudently to reach sustained profitability, with no date given. Some marquee advertisers may exit after sports, but some will stay if delivered value.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the fundraising and the 12/18-month timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Company wrote to the regulator seeking clarification with no response yet and has appealed to the Securities Appellate Tribunal. Management hopes for a quick resolution; preferential allotment approval is valid for one year but the matter is sub judice.

qa_highlights.question: How is the music business accounted for and is a demerger planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal transfer pricing governs music and digital P&Ls, and ZEE5 pays for music. Additional disclosures are being worked on. Demerger has been considered but is not being pursued absent a corporate action.

qa_highlights.question: How were FIFA rights payments structured and how much hits Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost value was not disclosed; payments are staggered over 8 years with a higher amount for the 2030 World Cup. A significant portion of FIFA revenue and cost lands in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Star arbitration?
qa_highlights.answer: Hearings held in July; final submissions due in about 1 to 1.5 months, with an outcome possibly in Q3 FY27. Further hearings are possible but not known.

risks_watch: Advertising recovery depends on festive season and West Asia; ad revenue fell 11% YoY in Q1.
Sustainability of FIFA-driven subscriber gains and content amortisation costs once the tournament ends.
Fundraising timeline under regulatory review and pending appeal at the Securities Appellate Tribunal.
Star arbitration outcome expected possibly in Q3 FY27.
Premium advertisers acquired for FIFA may not remain after the event.
Music business structure and disclosures remain unclear.

Management declined to give margin guidance and withheld several figures (FIFA cost, language-pack mix, B2B deals) as confidential, and deflected fundraising and music questions as sub judice or undecided.

505537|2026-09.headline: Zee Q2 FY27 operating revenue up 13% YoY, with FIFA-driven digital revenue doubling; EBITDA margin fell to 3.2% on new-initiative spends.
505537|2026-09.overview: Management reported 13% YoY growth in operating revenues, attributed mainly to the sports business (FIFA World Cup on ZEE5 and Unite8 Sports). ZEE5 revenues more than doubled YoY and grew 37% QoQ to INR6.3 billion, the highest quarterly digital revenue to date. EBITDA was INR708 million with a 3.2% margin, hit by FIFA programming and advertising costs and marketing spends on new initiatives (Bullet, KidZ, sports); management said the margin would have been mid-to-high single digit excluding those spends. PAT was INR456 million. Advertising was flat YoY and up 20% QoQ, and management said the ad decline has stabilised.

financial_highlights.value: Up 13% YoY (absolute figure not stated in call)

financial_highlights.change: Mid-to-high single digit ex new-initiative spends
After investments in sports and new initiatives

financial_highlights.value: INR25.7 billion (bank INR5.3bn, FDs and other INR11bn, mutual funds INR9.4bn)
financial_highlights.change: Includes first tranche of INR7.4bn from promoter preferential warrants
-36% YoY on higher syndication in base year

segments.name: Digital (ZEE5)
segments.commentary: Revenue more than doubled YoY and grew 37% QoQ to INR6.3 billion; digital EBITDA INR416 million after marketing and platform investments. Management expects digital momentum to continue in H2.

segments.name: Linear broadcast
segments.commentary: Management described the linear business as stable; network share was 20% as of week 24, the highest in seven years, but ratings measurement is currently paused. Management said linear subscription growth was stable and that the full sports benefit will show in FY28 as deals are fixed.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.commentary: Flat YoY, helped by FIFA, Sa Re Ga Ma Pa and new launches; up 20% QoQ as Middle East uncertainty eased. Festive season shifted into Q3 this year.

segments.name: Music
segments.commentary: Over 59 billion total video views and more than 179 million YouTube subscribers; management says profitability remains healthy. Segment disclosure is still withheld.

segments.name: Movies / studio
segments.commentary: Released six movies in Q2 (one Hindi, five other languages). Other sales and services fell 36% YoY against a higher syndication deal in the base year. Acquired international distribution rights to Drishyam 3, released in Q3.

segments.name: Sports
segments.commentary: FIFA full-tournament reach grew about 41% vs the previous World Cup, with about 83% of viewership live on ZEE5 and total reach above 400 million. Rights acquired to FIFA until 2034, plus Bundesliga and Serie A for five years.

guidance_outlook: Subscription revenue growth to accelerate from H2 onwards versus normalised levels, but not at the 30% seen in Q2 (management).
About 35% to 40% of FIFA-acquired subscribers retained after the event, with most renewing for another quarter or longer; accrual benefit continues through Q3 and Q4.
Management expects advertising revenue to hold without further decline in H2, with encouraging festive-season signs.
Digital growth momentum expected to continue in H2; marketing spends on new initiatives expected to pay off in H2 through subscription pack renewals.
Management said the true financial impact of new sports rights will be visible in FY28, since current linear deals are already fixed.
Management remains cautiously optimistic on FY27 revenue growth and profitability, citing festive season and content slate for Q3 and Q4.
capex_capacity: Ongoing investment in ZEE5 platform revamp across mobile and connected TV, with AI-led discovery and a stronger personalisation engine.
Bullet launched Trinetra AI, an end-to-end AI filmmaking and content intelligence platform aimed at the micro-drama segment.
Investment phase in kids, live experiences, animated content, micro dramas and sports, with new businesses still in investment mode.
Received INR7.4 billion, the first tranche of preferential warrant proceeds from promoters; FCCB repayment and dividend payout weighed on cash in the quarter.
demand_pricing: FIFA-driven subscriptions were mainly quarterly packs; revised FIFA pricing aided ZEE5 growth.
Linear pricing increases contributed to subscription growth, alongside digital ARPU and subscriber growth.
Omni reach across genres crossed 800 million monthly; ZEE5 released 34 shows and movies, including nine original series, in the quarter.
Advertising was flat YoY, and management cited high inflation and a weak monsoon as subdued macro headwinds.
Competition: management says Zee is India's number 2 TV entertainment network; it claims top digital engagement on YouTube and Meta in key language markets, per third-party data.

qa_highlights.question: How much did FIFA contribute to linear and ZEE5 revenue, and what would the quarter look like without it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not quantify FIFA revenue but said it was 'quite healthy', mostly booked as subscription. Linear revenue was stable, and the true sports benefit will show in FY28 because current deals are fixed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for withholding Zee Music segment disclosure, and is there a timeline for value unlocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working on segment reporting for the whole company rather than piecemeal and will revert when the time is right; it gave no timeline, citing investment-mode businesses.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the rise in receivables and inventories, and how did that affect cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said receivables are cyclical with no build-up affecting cash. Cash was mainly hit by the FCCB payment and dividend payout. Inventory includes show builds to be released in coming quarters, and inventory fell slightly QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: After FIFA, where will subscription growth settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Retention of FIFA subscribers is 35% to 40%, with renewals for quarterly and longer packs. Subscription growth will accelerate from normalised levels in H2, but not to 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Note 10 operating expense a one-off, and what is the status of legal cases?
qa_highlights.answer: Note 10 relates to a prior-year (Q4 FY26) transaction, shown for reference only, with no impact on Q2 margin. The main legal matter is the ICC case; management cannot predict timing for the LCIA arbitration.

505700|2026-03.headline: Elecon Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell to INR746 crore (from INR798 crore) as Gear sales dropped 21%; FY27 guidance held back.
505700|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue declined moderately YoY to INR746 crore, with EBITDA of INR158 crore (21.2% margin) and PAT of INR108 crore before a INR102 crore goodwill impairment. Gear Division revenue fell 21% YoY to INR472 crore on customer-led delivery deferrals, mainly in steel, while MHE grew 37% to INR274 crore. Management attributed the March shortfall to geopolitical-driven deferrals and said it will not give FY27 guidance, citing limited visibility. Open order book rose to about INR1,292 crore from INR948 crore a year earlier.

segments.name: Gear Division
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR472 crore (63% of consolidated) vs INR597 crore, down 21%; EBIT INR91 crore vs INR147 crore, margin about 19.3%. Q4 order intake INR550 crore; open order book INR894 crore at 31 March 2026 vs INR583 crore a year earlier.

segments.name: Material Handling Equipment (MHE)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR274 crore (37% of consolidated) vs INR200 crore, up 36.8%; EBIT INR62 crore vs INR59 crore. Q4 order inflow INR107 crore (described as a 10-quarter low); order book INR398 crore vs INR365 crore a year earlier.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 guidance; management is holding guidance and will revisit once the operating environment is clearer.
Management expects no degrowth vs FY26 in FY27; the growth rate is not quantified.
Management said that if domestic orders execute smoothly, EBITDA margin could return to the earlier 22%-24% range; no timeline given.
Sustainable MHE margin estimated at about 20%-22%.
Management said EBITDA margin should not be affected by the Gear-to-MHE mix shift in the long term.
Gear: about INR77 crore of March dispatches deferred (INR12 crore on hold, INR34 crore slipping to April, INR31 crore production put on hold); expected to clear in Q1 FY27.
Gear: a large order was described as at LOI stage and expected to convert within days; value not disclosed.
Indian Navy aircraft carrier RFP expected in Q1 FY27, orders now expected by Q4 FY27; P-17 Alpha deferred to around Q3 FY28.
capex_capacity: Capex plan of INR400 crore over FY26-FY28; about INR95 crore spent so far, with roughly 80% in Gear and the rest in MHE.
Capacity utilisation at about 56%-60% including recent capex additions.
About INR750-800 crore of capital employed sits in investments yielding about 8%; management is holding these pending clarity on expansion plans.
Established a step-down subsidiary in Mexico to serve Latin America and avoid the 50% US tariff; no significant capex planned there yet.
Four patents taken, three more under application; R&D spend continuing on new products.
demand_pricing: Export share about 18% of consolidated revenue in Q4 (domestic 82%); Middle East weakness noted, UAE overseas entity exposed to Strait of Hormuz disruption.
Q4 catalogue vs engineered mix (Gear): 55% catalogue and 45% engineered; FY26 mix 55:45 (catalogue:engineered). Management said engineered orders in hand at 31 March may execute next year.
MHE inquiry pipeline above INR1,000 crore across sectors; more than INR15 crore of orders received in April 2026.
Gear demand cited from power, steel and cement; sugar demand expected to rise on ethanol demand linked to crude supply concerns.
Input cost inflation: management said raw material was secured on order receipt and new orders are priced for higher raw material and logistics costs.
Receivables rose to about INR720 crore from about INR610 crore, with about INR70-75 crore linked to Feb-March sales not yet due and about INR15 crore overdue.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Gear-to-MHE mix moved to 63:37 from the historical 75:25, and does it affect EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said long-term margin should not vary, with mix possibly shifting further as both divisions grow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE outlook given ROCE fell from 29% in FY24 to 20.4% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR800 crore of capital employed is in investments yielding about 8%, and only about INR95 crore of the INR400 crore capex has been spent so far. Management expects capex to lift capacity and margins over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the goodwill impairment, and was there a tax benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR102 crore impairment relates to goodwill from the 2010-11 Benzler and Radicon acquisitions, held only in consolidated accounts. The tax deduction sits with the UK entity, with about GBP1 million of claims left over about five years.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 gear shortfall was caused by geopolitical events in March?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the impact was concentrated in March, with about INR70 crore of dispatches affected, and the Q4 revenue guidance cut of at least 5% had been flagged in January.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to the earlier 22%-24% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot commit to margin levels given the geopolitical situation, but if domestic orders execute smoothly, EBITDA margin could return to the earlier 22%-24% range.

qa_highlights.question: What are the sustainable margins for MHE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 20%-22% is sustainable, given the revenue mix.

505700|2026-06.headline: Elecon Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.9% YoY to INR521 crore, but management guided only low double-digit FY27 growth on raw-material-driven order conversion delays.
505700|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 11.9% YoY to INR521 crore over adjusted Q1 FY26 revenue of INR465 crore, with EBITDA up 3.9% to INR109 crore at a stated 21% margin and PAT of INR70 crore (13.5% margin, up 2.3%). Gear division drove growth, with revenue up 16.3% to INR416 crore, while MHE revenue fell 2.9% to INR105 crore on project execution delays and EBIT fell 25.3% to INR27 crore. Order intake rose 23% to INR755 crore and the consolidated open order book rose 36.8% to INR1,518 crore, yet management guided only low double-digit FY27 revenue growth, citing raw-material price spikes that slowed enquiry-to-order conversion and PSU-linked capex delays.

segments.name: Gear division
segments.commentary: Revenue INR416 crore (~80% of consolidated), up 16.3% YoY; order intake INR570 crore (+18.8%); open order book INR1,043 crore (+46.9%). EBIT INR75 crore at 17.9% margin vs FY26 full-year EBIT margin of 18.8%; mix 54% catalogue / 46% engineered.

segments.name: MHE division
segments.commentary: Revenue INR105 crore (-2.9% YoY) on project execution delays for power-sector orders; order intake INR185 crore (+38.1%); open order book INR475 crore (+18.8%). EBIT INR27 crore at about 25.6% margin vs FY26 full-year 24.7%; secured overseas port order of about INR21 crore.

segments.name: Overseas business
segments.commentary: Revenue INR151 crore (+21.9% YoY), led by Middle East and US; overseas order intake INR194 crore (+63%), including INR21 crore from MHE; overseas open order book INR256 crore (+73%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided to low double-digit percentage, described as conservative given macro uncertainty; management said it could be revisited next quarter.
Consolidated EBITDA margin to be maintained at the FY26 level (about 21%).
Gear division EBITDA margin guided to about 24%; gear EBIT margin expected around 19-20% over the next year and one year after.
MHE sustainable EBITDA margin guided at 22-24% for the year.
Exports expected to grow at least double digits in FY27; Europe recovery expected to take at least two quarters.
Mid-term FY30 revenue target of INR5,000 crore described as challenging but achievable, with Gear at 70-75% and MHE at 25-30% of revenue.
Gear revenue conversion expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 as stabilised prices are accepted; Q2 to show only gradual pick-up.
capex_capacity: Previously announced capex programme of approximately INR400 crore over FY26 to FY28 stated as on track; further capex under evaluation for board approval in near future.
Assembly centres outside India (Middle East, US and others) set up for customer proximity; some sub-assemblies locally outsourced.

Defence business has dedicated manufacturing and operating vertical built over the last 3-4 years; defence orders expected to execute over 2-3 years with working capital about 15-20% higher than the gear average.
Gear manufacturing cycle is 2-3 months for catalogue products and 4-5 months for engineered products.

505729|2026-03.headline: Singer India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 37% to Rs 166.3 crore and FY26 revenue reached Rs 557 crore, up 29%, led by Sewing Machines.
505729|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 166.3 crore (up 37%), PBT of Rs 8 crore (up 43%) and EBITDA of Rs 9.3 crore (up 49%). For FY26, revenue was Rs 557 crore (up 29%), EBITDA Rs 21.5 crore (up 70%) and PBT Rs 17.3 crore (up 73%), after a one-time labour code cost of Rs 73 lakh; adjusted EBITDA was Rs 22.2 crore and adjusted PBT Rs 18.1 crore. Sewing Machines drove growth, while Appliances revenue grew about 10% in Q4 but its segment result fell by about Rs 2 crore. Management gave no formal guidance and did not answer questions on promoter exit or M&A.

segments.name: Sewing Machines
segments.commentary: Grew about 45% in Q4 and more than 40% for FY26; trade channel up about 20% in Q4 and over 15% for the year. Zigzag up over 30%, industrial up over 13% in Q4 and over 20% for FY26, cast-iron straight stitch and accessories up over 50% for the year. E-commerce up over 50% in Q4 and about 30% for the year.

segments.name: Appliances
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 10% in Q4 on e-commerce range and fans, but segment result was lower by about Rs 2 crore due to EPR costs and fan business build-out. Demand muted, trade inventory blocked, dealer cash flows tight.

segments.name: Fans
segments.commentary: Fan business grew about 50% in Q4 with a new range covering economy, base, decorative, BLDC, TPW and exhaust fans; supply chain constrained by labour shortage and cost inflation.

guidance_outlook: Government (PMY) supply: more than 60% of the order completed; balance about 40% expected to be completed before the start of H2 FY27, though allocation timing has been revised.
Management intends to sustain sewing machine growth momentum but gave no numerical guidance.
Bhiwadi, Rajasthan factory (leased) expected to begin production in H2 FY27, initially focused on zigzag machines, with assembly first and components outsourced.
Management would not comment on future profits; said Appliances is expected to become profitable and that appliance challenges are temporary.
Management said the sewing machine business is expected to sustain growth, with the mix between sewing machines and appliances not expected to shift dramatically.
capex_capacity: Bhiwadi, Rajasthan factory: premises leased, production expected from H2 FY27, primarily zigzag machines; later capable of industrial machines and selected appliances.

demand_pricing: Management estimates the total Indian sewing machine market at about Rs 3,000 crore: about 55% industrial, about Rs 700 crore straight stitch household, about Rs 350 crore artisan and about Rs 250 crore zigzag (management's estimate; not formal data). Market growing 4-6%.
Company mix for FY26: zigzag about 20%, classic black machines about 55%, industrial and accessories about 28-30%.
High-speed machines account for nearly 50% of Indian market revenue, per management.

New innovative machines (DSBB, SLBB, Link etc.) are about 15% of household sewing machine category. Tailor Mate, a motorised straight-stitch machine priced near classic black machines, is gaining traction.
Raw material inflation: PMY government orders are fixed-price and cost increases must be absorbed. Labour shortage and steep commodity price rises disrupted supply and demand in Q4.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the orders are fixed-price and the company has to absorb the raw material cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will the fan business turn losses into breakeven in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no profit guidance; said fan sales grew about 50% in Q4, the heat is seasonal, and appliances will become profitable over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the government contract and when will it complete?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 60% of government supply is complete; the remaining 40% is expected before the start of H2 FY27. Growth came from government, retail and e-commerce.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for zigzag manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is phased and could reach Rs 90 crore over 3 years, but is not committed; the factory is leased and starts with assembly.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 not much higher than Q3 this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no specific reason; CFO said Q3 was about Rs 160 crore and Q4 about Rs 165 crore, and growth is expected to be sustainable.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply depends on allocations received; initial allocation estimates have been revised to a different pace. The second PMY order will come when government issues it.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the dividend should be seen in the context of a profitable journey and that cash will be deployed in opportunities, with no timeline. CFO said ROCE is almost 10%, with working capital improvement and the Bhiwadi capex ahead.

505729|2026-06.headline: Singer India Q1 FY27 revenue rose 57% to Rs 144.5 crore and EBITDA rose 330% to Rs 5.5 crore, with sewing machines up 74%.
505729|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue up 57% to Rs 144.5 crore, PBT up 225% to Rs 4 crore and EBITDA up 330% to Rs 5.5 crore. Sewing machines grew 74% and the trade channel grew more than 25%, while appliances grew about 15% but its segment result fell by about Rs 74 lakh YoY on EPR costs and organisation build-out. Management said a sharp commodity price rise disrupted demand and sourcing in the quarter. Working capital absorbed cash for ZigZag and industrial machine imports and inventory, with closing cash at about Rs 58 crore.

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash before working capital changes

segments.name: Sewing machines
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 74% in Q1, with the trade channel up more than 25%, e-commerce up more than 55% and ZigZag machines up more than 20%. Revenue mix in the quarter was about 20% ZigZag, 50% black machines and 30% industrial machines and accessories.

segments.name: Appliances
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 15% from trade expansion, e-commerce and fans, but segment result fell about Rs 74 lakh YoY on EPR and organisation build-out. Fans grew about 61%; coolers underperformed while induction cooktops helped.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for EBIT-level breakeven in appliances, which it now expects next year rather than this fiscal.
Bhiwadi, Rajasthan factory on track for pilot production in the second half of FY27, initially focused on ZigZag machines, with initial capacity of 10,000+ machines per month.
Kendriya Bhandar order (Rs 202 crore) targeted for completion by end of the quarter; the contract has a 25% volume scale-up clause.
Industrial sewing machine growth expected to be high in coming periods, though Q1 was damped by a steep price correction.
Dividend policy not addressed; management said the Board is aware of investor expectations.
capex_capacity: Bhiwadi factory is being set up as asset light at first, focused on skill building, then in-house component manufacturing, then industrial sewing machines.
Advances of about Rs 14.3 crore to Singer Sourcing LLC for ZigZag machine imports and about Rs 4 crore for industrial machine imports, at 30% advance with 70% on bill of lading.
Total inventory and import deployment of about Rs 32 crore in the quarter, plus inventory build in fans.
New Jammu factory has started making Made-in-India ZigZag machines compliant with the revised BIS standard IS 15449.
demand_pricing: Commodity price spike caused demand disruption, labour shortage and sourcing challenges; a steep price correction was taken, which dampened demand in appliances and industrial machines.
Management says it is gaining market share, with consistent growth across channels and categories.

Revised BIS standard IS 15449 took full effect on 12 August 2026; management says Singer is the only company manufacturing ZigZag machines to the new standard in India and no further NOCs or imports will be allowed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Kendriya Bhandar order's pending balance and scale-up potential clear?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to complete the order by quarter end and declined to give the pending value, citing competitive sensitivity. It said a 25% volume expansion and a larger future tender are possible but depend on government decisions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EPR cost and why are appliances profits weak?
qa_highlights.answer: EPR is about Rs 1.2 crore for the quarter, which is proportionate for the year and relates to past sales. Management aims for appliances EBIT breakeven and expects it to cover the cost.

qa_highlights.question: How much cash was generated and what is the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating cash before working capital changes was Rs 4.35 crore. About Rs 32 crore went into inventory and import advances, and closing cash is about Rs 58 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 100 crore surplus enough for inorganic growth and the factory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is open to inorganic deals but will only pursue good opportunities. The factory will be built in stages, and it said more funds will come if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why import ZigZag machines when local manufacturing has started?
qa_highlights.answer: Imports were allowed until 12 August. The Rs 14.3 crore of advances was described as de-risking inventory while domestic production ramps up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split and export plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The mix is about 20% ZigZag, 50% black machines and 30% industrial machines and accessories. Exports are a lower priority than India, though SVP Global may buy machines for its global supply chain.

risks_watch: Commodity cost inflation and price corrections may keep dampening demand in appliances and industrial sewing machines.

ZigZag manufacturing learning curve: management says the capacity ramp is still in progress, and the import stock build reflects that.
Working capital absorbed cash in Q1, so cash conversion needs watching.

505790|2026-03.headline: Schaeffler India Q1 CY26 revenue rose 18.8% YoY to INR 2,507 crore, with EBITDA of INR 483 crore (19.3% margin) and PAT of INR 319.7 crore.
505790|2026-03.overview: Revenue grew 18.8% YoY to INR 2,507 crore but fell 5.1% QoQ as management recalibrated the bearings and industrial portfolio and some sectors saw liquidity-driven offtake weakness. EBITDA held at INR 483 crore (19.3% margin, up 18.6% YoY) and PAT rose 12.8% YoY to INR 319.7 crore. Automotive Technologies (+30.8% YoY) and exports (+32.5% YoY) drove growth, while Bearings and Industrial Solutions was up only 4.2% YoY and down 14.3% QoQ. Management flagged supply-chain and fuel-cost pressure from the West Asia crisis, with price recovery expected over about six quarters.

vs INR 237 crore in Q1 CY25; lower QoQ

segments.name: Automotive Technologies
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 30.8% YoY and fell 1.3% QoQ; about 37% of sales. Growth came from ICE clutch and engine systems, with hybrid also strong; new wins in transmission, heavy-duty clutches and hydraulic cam phasers.

segments.name: Bearings and Industrial Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 4.2% YoY but fell 14.3% QoQ; about 35% of sales. Management cited recalibration, supply-chain disruption and an aftermarket liquidity squeeze; industrial bearings estimated at about 60% localised.

segments.name: Vehicle Lifetime Solutions
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 18.1% YoY and fell 0.6% QoQ; about 12% of sales.

segments.name: Exports (intercompany)

Management sees no major concern in delivering this year's committed numbers, but says monitoring and agility are required given supply-chain uncertainty.

Price increases to recover input costs start from Q2; full recovery takes 6-18 months, close to six quarters.

demand_pricing: Automotive demand strong: about 2.5 million two-wheelers and over 0.5 million cars produced in March 2026 alone, per management.
Bearings: management cited competitive intensity from local capacity build-out, leading to pricing pressure and a portfolio recalibration at the start of the year.

Aftermarket industrial demand slowed because of a liquidity crunch at distributors, with a seasonal Q1 effect that management expects to reverse next quarter. Railways and power transmission were described as stable to good; mining was weak.

Fuel and LPG costs rose after West Asia supply disruption; mitigation via alternate sourcing, stockpiling and seeking customer compensation. Too early to quantify (about 1.5 months since the increase).
Exports are mainly to group companies in Europe, China, Southeast Asia and the Americas; management sees no demand dip.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CY26 outlook for industrial segments such as wind, railways and off-road?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no major concerns in delivering this year's committed numbers, though supply-chain uncertainty from the Middle East requires daily crisis management meetings.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the roughly 31% Automotive Technologies growth, well above underlying production growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Strong traction across ICE, hybrid and e-mobility platforms; almost all ICE product lines grew strongly in Q1, and management expects the automotive trend to stay robust.

qa_highlights.question: Why did bearings stay flat to down, and is demand or competition the cause?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited localisation, product and market mix recalibration, rising competitor activity and pricing pressure, plus an aftermarket liquidity squeeze; it said the recalibration was done at the start of the year.

qa_highlights.question: How are the export geographies performing?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe, China, Southeast Asia and the Americas are all stable with no demand dip; the order book shows at least 10% growth for the year.

qa_highlights.question: How long does it take to pass on input cost increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases begin in Q2; full recovery takes 6-18 months, close to six quarters, under the price-excellence mechanism.

qa_highlights.answer: Yes, there was an inventory buildup in the quarter; management expects better inventory levels in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 2026 capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 400-500 crore in CY26, with a pickup toward about INR 500 crore after the FY25 rationalisation.

505790|2026-09.headline: Schaeffler India says automotive demand is growing about 29-30% on GST 2.0 and localization is at 80%, with no explicit numbers on Q2 FY27 financials.
505790|2026-09.overview: This was an investor group meeting (Sept 28, 2026), not a formal results call, so no quarterly financial figures were given. Management said automotive growth of roughly 29-30% was driven by GST 2.0 and BS-VI product transitions, while industrial growth was mixed, with infrastructure, steel, cement and railways strong and construction equipment and mining weak. Exports were framed as a by-product of localization, with management targeting 15-20% of revenue from exports. Management said the West Asia conflict raised input costs, with about 70% of cost increases typically recovered from customers, and that Vitesco's India integration has no timeline. E-mobility was described as loss-making and early-stage, with adoption under 5% today and about 15% expected by FY31.

segments.commentary: Mixed: steel, cement and infrastructure strong, renewables (wind) growing, railways booming; construction equipment fell last year and mining has not recovered; industrial growth described as single digit.

qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 50% Europe (intercompany), 25% Southeast Asia, with the rest China and the Americas; 13% of exports go to China. Exports are a by-product of localization, with the company expecting 15-20% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How does the West Asia conflict affect costs and demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the crisis hits industrial exports and input costs (fuel, LPG), not automotive demand. About 70% of cost increases are typically recovered, with the remaining 30% absorbed by efficiencies.

qa_highlights.question: Where does Vitesco stand and is there an integration timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said there is no legal hurdle, but there is no timeline. Parent holds 74.13%, with 26% public; the group must integrate Vitesco entities worldwide first.

qa_highlights.question: How are EV economics and competition shaping up?
qa_highlights.answer: EV is loss-making at start; profitability depends on volume. EV adoption is below 5% today and about 15% by 2030-31 per internal research; hybrids are expected at about 15% by 2031.

qa_highlights.question: Is Vitesco's e-axle content imported, and what does Vitesco bring?
qa_highlights.answer: The e-axle is a Schaeffler portfolio product, with the CFO noting 100% import content at Phase 1. Vitesco adds BMS, sensors (NOx, knock) and power electronics; 800-volt capability is now under development.

qa_highlights.question: Is railway demand secular or lumpy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tendering-driven lumpiness will persist; electrification and the move to larger loads (Vande Bharat, freight Class K bearings) add structural demand.

qa_highlights.question: Is automotive running at maximum utilisation, and can growth sustain into FY27-28?

506194|2026-03.headline: Arihant Superstructures Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 18.5% YoY to Rs 181 crore; FY26 EBITDA margin 23% and FY27 margin guided to 25-27%.

506222|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 51.9% to INR126 crores and PAT rose 58.6% to INR84.3 crores, despite total income down 6.3%.
506222|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 total income fell 6.3% to INR658 crores while EBITDA rose 51.9% to INR126 crores, with margin up 734 bps to 19.2%. Management attributed the stronger profitability to product mix (lower GPPS volumes) and opportunistic pricing in tight segments, and said there was no significant inventory gain. Volumes fell 4.6% YoY to 46.1 KT, driven by GPPS weakness, while ABS and HIPS grew. Management declined to quantify the Thailand breakeven change or the power-savings benefit, citing short-term market distortion from the Middle East supply crisis, and reiterated that India ABS capacity additions remain on track for the second half of FY27.

segments.name: HIPS (India)

Raw material (styrene, acrylonitrile) and finished product prices rose globally in tandem; management says there is no significant regional arbitrage.
ABS spot prices were quoted at about INR190-200 per kg versus INR110-120 pre-war, per an analyst; management said prices will likely stay somewhat higher in the short-to-medium term.
Management said Q4 profitability was helped by mix and opportunistic pricing in tight segments, which it does not view as sustainable.
Large OE customers in automotive, appliances and packaging continue to buy steadily; demand is muted at current prices and weaker among unorganized and smaller buyers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Thailand breakeven utilisation (65-70%) now easier to reach given current pricing and raw material availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said breakeven targets should not change; short-term tightness gains are arbitrage that may not last. Thailand still needs to reach 60-70% utilisation to generate returns.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 volume drop in India and the 20-30% drop in Thailand explained?
qa_highlights.answer: India dip was from GPPS only; ABS and HIPS grew YoY. Thailand comparison was distorted by prior-year pre-buying ahead of the INEOS-to-Styrenix brand switch, and Jan-Mar is seasonally weaker. Most business was retained.

qa_highlights.question: Is the spread at spot prices better or worse in FY27 versus FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract and formula margins are similar or slightly better. Spot margins are better for specific grades where Korean suppliers' quality is weak, but this is opportunistic.

qa_highlights.question: Should capex be preponed for ABS given Korean import disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said capex is proceeding as planned with no acceleration.

qa_highlights.question: What share of sales is formula-based versus spot?
qa_highlights.answer: ABS: 60-70% formula or contract. HIPS: well above 50% formula/OEM. GPPS: formula-based pricing above 70% for the business overall, with volumes dropping as the company avoids unformulated segments.

qa_highlights.question: Will Thailand ever reach breakeven given normalised spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated that returns start at 60-70% utilisation and the plant is still below that level.

506222|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 133.9% to INR201.4 crore (26.1% margin) even as sales volume fell 26% to 38.9 KT.
506222|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income grew 6.6% to INR770.5 crore and PAT rose 150.3% to INR137.3 crore, driven by a sharp margin jump, while volumes dropped 26% as non-OEM buyers held back amid Middle East-driven raw material price volatility. Consolidated (India plus Thailand) volume was 50.8 KT, EBITDA INR223.6 crore at 22% margin. Management described the margin gain as a snapshot of a volatile quarter, not a sustainable run rate, and gave no volume guidance. The ABS capacity expansion is said to be on track for completion in FY27 without a firm commissioning month, and Thailand volumes remain subdued.

segments.name: ABS (India)
segments.commentary: Demand fell in the quarter, with a smaller drop than polystyrene; OEM is about 70% or more of ABS sales. Management did not give a segment volume split.

segments.name: Polystyrene (India)
segments.commentary: Hit harder than ABS, mainly in the non-OEM/unorganised segment; OEM is about 50% of PS sales. Management did not give volume numbers.

segments.name: SAN
segments.commentary: Merchant sales run at about 15,000-20,000 tonnes a year against roughly 100,000 tonnes of capacity; most output is used captively, and merchant sales will continue after the ABS expansion.

segments.name: Thailand
segments.commentary: Running at low utilisation on specific products; volumes were broadly maintained quarter on quarter, but new business has not yet translated into meaningful volume growth. Validation cycles run 12-24 months.

guidance_outlook: No volume guidance given; management said it is 'virtually impossible' to forecast given the current environment.
Management said Q1 margins are not indicative of sustainable performance; for modelling, assume margins similar to the existing business, with the expansion adding volume.
ABS expansion (about 50,000 tonnes in the chemical plant) to be completed in FY27; exact commissioning month not given.

No new capex or capital allocation changes beyond the ABS expansion; polystyrene expansion to be decided when the business case is clearer.
capex_capacity: ABS expansion is a brownfield project at a running site, so commissioning is complex; management expects completion within FY27.
SAN capacity of about 100,000 tonnes against merchant sales of 15-20 KT a year; expansions planned across rubber, SAN and compounding sites.
Thailand cost base is described as higher than India's; no reduction timeline was given.
demand_pricing: Demand fell in Q1 due to a Middle East-driven price spike from March and high volatility; buyers in the non-OEM/unorganised segment held back. Management put the volume decline at about 15-25% on total polymer.

Styrene monomer went from about $1,000/t pre-war to $1,600-1,700, then about $1,200, and has since traded in a $1,100-1,400 range. Acrylonitrile moved from $1,200 to about $1,800-1,900 and is now $1,400-1,600. Butadiene (bought locally) went from $1,000 to above $2,500 and has since eased.
Styrene monomer is now sourced from alternate suppliers with 10-15 days longer lead times; management said it is 'fully covered' and carried slightly higher raw material inventory at quarter end.
Price pass-through is handled through short-term mechanisms and global price markers; management said previous-quarter pricing was significantly higher and moderated toward quarter end.
Imports: management said it has seen no significant change in import volumes, with some Asian exporters constrained by energy and naphtha shortages. Official import data is not available.

qa_highlights.question: How much did demand fall in India for ABS and PS, and was it driven by non-OEM buyers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the volume decline was in line across ABS and PS, roughly 15-25% on total polymer. The non-OEM segment was hit harder than OEM, which was affected only muted.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin once the Q1 benefit reverses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was a snapshot of an unusual event and is not indicative of sustainable earnings; pre-event performance is the right base. It did not give a number.

qa_highlights.question: Will SAN merchant sales stop after ABS expansion, and what is the capex timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: SAN merchant sales will continue. The ABS expansion will be completed in FY27, but exact timing was not disclosed because the project runs alongside an operating plant.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any new capital allocation plan given extra cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no new plan; cash will go to planned capex with the rest returned to shareholders in line with existing policy. No specific dividend or buyback was announced.

qa_highlights.question: What are Thailand's volume and sales plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Thailand sales strategy is to win validations in China, Japan, Vietnam, Korea and others; validations take 12-24 months. No volume guidance was given.

Recovery of non-OEM volumes and whether destocking or channel stock effects reverse in the next nine months.
ABS expansion timing (within FY27) and execution risk on a brownfield site.
Thailand utilisation and validation progress; cost base still above India's.
Raw material lead times and alternate sourcing for styrene monomer and acrylonitrile; freight and energy disruptions.
Limited import data availability, which makes competitive import pressure hard to track.

506222|2026-09.headline: Styrenix Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 3.3% to INR84.5 crore on 10.8% margin, while Thailand remains loss-making and India capacity expansion is due by FY27 end.

H1 standalone EBITDA grew 70% to INR286 crore (18.4% margin) on 82.4 KT. Consolidated Q2 EBITDA was INR75.6 crore (7.6% margin), with the gap to standalone attributed to the Thailand subsidiary. Management said ABS volumes recovered after a disrupted Q1, while GPPS volumes were deliberately reduced to avoid speculative styrene purchases; Phase 1 expansion remains on track for FY27 end.

506395|2026-03.headline: Coromandel Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19% to INR 6,068 crore and EBITDA 16% to INR 494 crore, but reported PAT fell to INR 115 crore on last year's land-sale gain.

506401|2026-06.headline: Deepak Nitrite Q1 FY27: record consolidated EBITDA of INR 554 crore (21% margin) and PAT of INR 345 crore, up 207% YoY.
506401|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 35% YoY and 22% QoQ to INR 2,592 crore, with EBITDA up 159% YoY to INR 554 crore and margin at 21% versus 11% a year ago. Phenolics delivered record EBIT of INR 418 crore at a 24% margin, while Advanced Intermediates EBIT was INR 67 crore at an 8% margin. Management said April was disrupted by a maintenance shutdown, propylene shortages and gas curtailment, so the phenol run rate of about 1 lakh tonnes applies to parts of the quarter rather than the full period. Debt funding for the INR 11,500 crore propylene-polycarbonate project has been closed, and the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.27x.

segments.name: Phenolics
segments.commentary: Record revenue of INR 1,775 crore and EBIT of INR 418 crore (24% margin), supported by stronger realisations, sustained demand and high utilisation. Management said the business is almost entirely domestic.

segments.name: Advanced Intermediates (AI)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR 804 crore and EBIT of INR 67 crore (8% margin), helped by better realisations, higher operating rates and product mix. AI export mix is about 40-50%; raw material costs stayed high for some products.

guidance_outlook: MIBK and MIBC to be commissioned with acetophenone in August 2026; the remaining projects (multipurpose agrochemical intermediates facility, etc.) are due in Q2 FY27, with commercial volumes from January.
Management aims to reach 4 lakh tonnes of phenol in the existing Deepak Phenolics asset in the short to medium term, with about INR 70-odd crore of debottlenecking capex.
Polycarbonate commissioning targeted for H2 FY28-29 and BPA a couple of months later; propylene from the PDH project is expected to support phenol volumes.

Capex: about INR 1,200 crore spent to date, another INR 1,000-1,600 crore in FY27 (figures varied in the call), and about INR 3,000 crore in FY28. Peak debt estimated at INR 8,000-8,500 crore including working capital, with D/E below 1.
capex_capacity: Ammonia-to-amines integration chain (nitric acid plant, nitration and reduction) completed and stabilised; the company says it now runs 8 products simultaneously.

Phenol capacity is about 3.5 lakh tonnes, and management says it is debottlenecking toward 4 lakh tonnes through advanced process controls. Run rate reached about 1 lakh tonnes per quarter in parts of Q1, but was not sustained through the full quarter.
MIBC pre-commissioning runs reportedly exceeded design capacity; management said it can ramp above 100% once demand comes in.
Debt for the INR 11,500 crore propylene-polycarbonate project is closed, funded 60:40 debt to equity, with the 25% equity already contributed.
demand_pricing: Management said phenol demand in India is roughly balanced with no new global capacity, and some supply is short. Imports were duty-free for most of Q1 until the government reimposed the duty.
Raw material costs were high in April, but procurement secured feedstock for continuous operations. Management said feedstock costs are competitive domestically and globally.
Freight and insurance costs rose. The company responded with CIF to FOB shifts, larger parcels, and a product reformulation for a Middle East customer that changed its hazard class.
Consolidated export mix is about 20%. AI is roughly 50-50 domestic to export; Phenolics is almost entirely domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Is the phenol supply-demand balance sound?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no new capacity, China is largely self-sufficient, demand is balanced and India is short of supply.

qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,200 crore has been spent. Peak borrowing is about INR 6,800 crore plus working capital, for total peak debt of INR 8,000-8,500 crore. Management said D/E will stay below 1x.

506405|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose to INR 177 crore from INR 150 crore QoQ, mostly raw-material pass-through; FY26 revenue INR 582 crore.
506405|2026-03.overview: Management attributed the quarter's sharp top-line rise to pass-through of higher sulfur and boron raw-material prices rather than volume, and said absolute margins were maintained though percentage margins fell. Sulfur supply was constrained by Middle East/Hormuz disruption, and the Roha plant ran at about 60% capacity for roughly 15 days in March before supply was restored. Working capital and short-term borrowings rose substantially on higher inventory, debtor and advance-payment requirements for boron, at about 8.75-9% interest. Management declined to give quantified guidance beyond saying FY27 specialty utilisation should be better than FY26.

506590|2026-03.headline: PCBL Q4 FY26 carbon black volume rose 8% YoY to 161,865 MT while consolidated EBITDA was INR248 crores; management guides double-digit FY27 EBITDA growth.

506590|2026-09.headline: PCBL Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% YoY to INR 2,474 crores and PAT 20% to INR 74 crores, despite carbon black volumes of 134,180 tonnes.
506590|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14% YoY to INR 2,474 crores, EBITDA rose 12% to INR 310 crores and PAT grew 20% to INR 74 crores, on pricing discipline and cost actions. Carbon black volumes were weak as management let go of low-margin spot and Southeast Asian orders, and the company said it would not chase volume. Management kept the EBITDA-per-tonne guidance but flagged that the volume growth target of about 7% is now challenging. Crude moved back above $100 during the quarter, which lifted realisations, and Russian CBFS supply disruption is expected to keep feedstock tight.

Management expects a strong H2 but says the timing of recovery depends on market conditions; buying patterns expected to improve gradually.
INR 200-250 crore cost-saving programme (Project Alchemy) still targeted, with INR 10-15 crores captured so far; acceleration expected from coming quarters.
Coal distillation (backward integration) capex, part of INR 300 crore FY27 capex plan, is in final approval; announcement expected shortly.
Antidumping duty on HEDP and ATMP is provisional; not included in Aquapharm forecasts.

Super Conductive Black facility commissioned; Acetylene Black on track under the ECMS framework.
Nanovace (51% JV with Kinaltek) pilot at Palej producing samples now in internal qualification; silicon carbon composite development across Palej, Belgium and Australia.
US railcar infrastructure and Antwerp warehouse being set up to support export volumes.
Management said it may slightly postpone some capex decisions if needed.

Price increase announced in the spot market, with further increases expected in November and December.
Russian refinery throughput at multi-decade lows, keeping global CBFS tight; Chinese coal tar prices firmed, supporting SE Asia prices.
Russian and Chinese imports into India declining over recent months as Russian supply tightened and Chinese coal tar costs rose.
Customers destocked in Q2; some tyre customers who stocked up in Q1 are expected to return volume in Q3.

Feedstock: about 80-85% previously sourced from the Gulf; US mix unchanged, with diversification to multiple US vendors and sourcing from Southeast Asia under negotiation, with a possible 1-2% premium on that volume.

Europe market growth expected at about 1-2% next year; US tariff volatility still restraining large customers from shifting volumes.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said crude stayed elevated rather than falling back, so there was no inventory give-back, with only about INR 10-15 crores of Q1 gains passed through early in Q2. Spot price increases are in place and further increases are expected in November and December.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power revenue fall, and what drives power generation?

qa_highlights.question: Cost reduction quantification and outlook under the INR 200-250 crore programme?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of the fixed cost decline was volume-driven, with about INR 10-15 crores from Project Alchemy so far. Management expects acceleration as initiatives are standardised over the coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Export volume outlook for FY27 and the likely contribution from new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a return to international growth as coal tar prices rise, with US railcar infrastructure unlocking volume. It expects significant export growth over the next few years through long-term tie-ups.

qa_highlights.question: Volume guidance after a weak Q2?

qa_highlights.answer: About INR 19,800 per tonne EBITDA, of which about INR 2,300 was the US tariff refund, giving roughly INR 17,500 per tonne excluding the refund.

506618|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to INR326.7 crore, but gross margin fell to 34.1% and PAT to INR13.5 crore (4.1% margin).

Gross margin compressed about 540 bps to 34.1% from raw material inflation and new-product learning-curve effects. EBITDA rose 12.6% to INR29.6 crore at a 9% margin. H1 PAT fell 9.3% to INR35.5 crore because about INR9 crore of prior-year other income (FX gains and tax-refund interest) did not recur. Management said deferred export orders should flow into Q3 and Q4.

506655|2026-03.headline: Sudarshan Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA INR73 crore, business EBITDA INR118 crore; net debt cut to INR755 crore from INR934 crore in Dec-25.

segments.commentary: Q4 business EBITDA EUR11 million, with FY26 EBITDA turning positive on value capture. Management guides EUR35 million EBITDA for FY27 and EUR90-100 million over 3-4 years. Gross margin is 4-5 percentage points above Legacy, offset by higher fixed costs.

506655|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs.2,642 Cr and business EBITDA Rs.247 Cr for One Sudarshan; FY27 guidance held pending Q2 review.

506687|2026-06.headline: Transpek Q1 FY27 revenue fell 6.5% YoY to INR155.1 crore and EBITDA fell 32.4% to INR24.1 crore, with a 15.6% margin.
506687|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR155.1 crore, down 6.5% YoY, with EBITDA of INR24.1 crore (down 32.4% YoY) and a 15.6% margin, and PAT of INR8.9 crore. Management attributed the decline to aggressive pricing, oversupply and subdued export demand. The company remains net debt-free. Management said it is moving to a more aggressive growth stance, with an Odisha greenfield site (INR250 crore over 5-6 years, subject to board approval) and a multi-purpose pilot plant at Ekalbara. The DuPont contract, now assigned to Arclin, continues on unchanged terms, with renewal talks expected between Q4 CY26 and Q1 CY27.

segments.name: Polymers (end-user application)
segments.commentary: Largest end-user segment at 48.7% of Q1 revenue; down from 60-65% a few years ago to roughly 45-50% over time as the portfolio diversified.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: 22.5% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: 10.11% of Q1 revenue.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: 18.7% of Q1 revenue; management cited rising contribution from organic peroxides, dyes and surfactants during the quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at least 15% over FY26 (about 15-20% stated), with acid chloride sales to rise from about INR4 crore to about INR15 crore this year.
Target to double business size in 5 years; management said the strategy is finalised.
EBITDA margin guided at 15-20% going forward, with product-wise margins varying.

New products: one product expected to add about INR50 crore annual revenue, with commercialisation near year-end FY27 and revenue from next year; a second product expected to add about INR50 crore annually; several others could add INR50-100 crore each.
Odisha greenfield project: board decision targeted within 25-30 days; construction could start by end-November 2026 if approved; commercial production 1.5-2 years after start; payback 4-5 years.
Multi-purpose pilot plant at Ekalbara: 6-7 months to build, around February 2027.
Management said the company expects to run all four sites at full permitted capacity this quarter.
capex_capacity: Odisha greenfield capex of about INR250 crore over 5-6 years in multiple phases, pending board approval and feasibility study; DuPont-linked capex in the past was about INR110 crore.
Multi-purpose pilot plant (four streams, multi-step chemistry, fluorination, distillation) being built at Ekalbara; about 6-7 months to complete.
Effective capacity utilisation of about 70-75% (best case 80-82%) because capacity is product-specific and permits are 20-30% below the sum of stream capacities.
Expansion blocked at Ekalbara (about 10 years of approvals pending) and Dahej (about 1.5 years for permissions). Of three job-work sites, two are in the same Ekalbara area.
Management said about INR200 crore of capex over the last 5-6 years was largely replacement and captive thionyl chloride capacity, not growth capex.
demand_pricing: Pricing pressure from Indian and global competitors; price erosion in some products. Open-market acid chloride pricing is competitive, while Arclin pricing is formula-based cost-plus.

Arclin (ex-DuPont) contract assigned in full with the same terms. Management said Arclin's order volumes are rising this quarter, and the contract is a pass-through for raw materials; rupee depreciation is passed on to the customer.
Management said it is in talks with about 2 customers on sizeable contracts, but decisions are being delayed.
Electronics-grade trimethylbenzoyl chloride (TMBC/246 TMBC, for photoinitiators) is being developed for one large customer; purification work is ongoing.
Management said there were no product discontinuations, though some product demand fell sharply in certain quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Growth has lagged the 10-12% CAGR previously guided (FY19 revenue INR595 crore vs FY26 INR621 crore, EBITDA INR117 crore vs INR80 crore); would the company consider a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said estimates are not guaranteed due to cycles, guided at least 15% revenue growth for FY27, and said the board sees buybacks as lower-return than reinvesting in growth.

qa_highlights.question: What happens if the Arclin/DuPont contract is not renewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no reason for non-renewal (nine-year supplier, no rejected kilos, no missed deliveries) but is preparing for a worst case; a non-renewal would be a significant blow to volume and margins, with recovery taking time.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the INR300 crore Silox investment not being monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stake is illiquid under the shareholder agreement; the partner has been offered the stake but has not bought it, and no near-term resolution is expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US tariff advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no special tariff; Transpek pays the normal 18% rate, and customers receive duty drawbacks.

qa_highlights.question: Why expand capacity when utilisation is only 70-75%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said permissions at Ekalbara are blocked, product-specific streams require a mix, and Odisha is needed for new products.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex now being committed ahead of demand, and what revenue do the new products add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is investing partly ahead of demand. It said two products could add about INR50 crore each annually, and that the INR150-200 crore guided earlier had not yet materialised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected IRR or payback on the INR250 crore Odisha project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said payback would be 4-5 years.

Margin pressure from competition and from volatile raw material prices (management cited a jump from about $2,600/t to $4,000/t within 10 days).
Odisha board approval and permit timing; the 2 to 1.5 year execution timeline is long.
New product commercialisation has slipped in the past (a battery electrolyte product was stopped after a technology change).
Silox stake (about INR300 crore) remains illiquid with no near-term monetisation.
Management said the West Asia conflict and logistics are a risk to global demand.

506767|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue and profit were flat (within ±1% YoY); management sees margin improvement next year but guides only 5-10% volume growth.
506767|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as challenging, with both top line and bottom line roughly flat YoY, and volume down about 1% and prices down about 1%. The March 2026 ammonia sourcing disruption from the Middle East war was short-lived, with inventories bridging the gap and plants kept running at roughly 60-85% utilisation. Ammonia cost rose from about INR50/kg to over INR100/kg, and the company passed through price increases, with aceto prices now above INR200/kg versus about INR140-150/kg last year. Management believes the margin trough has passed but cautioned that gains from price pass-through are temporary and that competition will settle margins later.

financial_highlights.value: Roughly flat; combined volume and price decline about 2%
About 1% above last year; capacity 2 lakh tons, output about 110,000 tons per analyst estimate (not confirmed by management)

financial_highlights.change: Up roughly 30-40% from last year's average of INR140-150/kg
Up from about INR50/kg before the war

segments.name: Ethylamines
segments.commentary: Margins have improved as alcohol prices rose and prices stabilised; management says the market is a duopoly with Balaji and has enough capacity for 4-5 years. Market share is stable.

segments.name: Methylamines
segments.commentary: Still under pressure from new capacity: Aarti Industries commissioned a plant, taking the domestic players to four (RCF, Balaji, Aarti, Alkyl Amines). Management expects overcapacity and low utilisation to persist for some time.

segments.name: Acetonitrile (aceto)
segments.commentary: Anti-dumping duty came into effect only towards end-FY26 after Chinese pipeline imports. Chinese prices have risen and imports fallen in the last quarter, with market share gains. Company has about 30,000 tons capacity across two plants and says it will be the lowest-cost producer.

segments.name: End-user mix
segments.commentary: Pharma is 50-60% of sales and agro 15-20%, together about 70-75%. Management sees no pharma slowdown yet but flagged agro risk from a possible El Nino monsoon.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth guided at 5-10% for the next year, in line with expected industry growth of about 5-7%; value growth higher because of elevated prices.
Management expects some margin improvement next year, but says it is difficult to predict continued growth beyond that.
Raw material and finished goods prices are not expected to return to pre-February 2026 levels soon; supply-chain normalisation is expected to take 3-6 months.
Kurkumbh project commissioning slipped to the beginning of Q2 FY27 from April-June 2026; mechanical completion expected by end-June; economics unchanged.
FY27-28 capex estimated at INR80-90 crore, mainly the balance of the Dahej new product plant and engineering projects; maintenance capex INR20-30 crore per year.
A product launch from the R&D pipeline is expected in July 2026; further R&D investment decisions deferred until volatility settles.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation at most plants is about 60-85%; enough capacity for the next few years without new investment in existing products.
Ethylamines: large plant built 3-4 years ago, adequate for 4-5 years of growth; debottlenecking possible.
Acetonitrile: about 30,000 tons capacity across two plants, sufficient for a couple of years. Balaji is building an 18,000 ton ACN plant this year.
Kurkumbh project delayed by about one quarter; mechanical completion expected end-June 2026.

Gross margin compressed to 32.5% from 39% a year earlier and 37% in Q1, while PAT rose about 11% YoY to INR19 crores. Management attributed the margin dip to higher realizations diluting percentage margins, a roughly 45-day lag in passing through sulphur and fluorspar costs, and early-stage ramp-up of new products. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 35-40% and guided H2 EBITDA margin to about 18%, with HFC-32 commissioning targeted for Q3 FY27.

segments.name: AHF (anhydrous hydrofluoric acid)

segments.name: Solar grade DHF
segments.commentary: Capacity raised from 20,000 to 25,000 MT per annum via debottlenecking at nominal capex; utilisation rose from 80-85% in Q1 to 90-95% in Q2. Pricing is contractual with a roughly 45-day lag on raw material pass-through.

segments.name: HFC-32 (R-32) refrigerant gas
segments.commentary: Plant about 90% complete with about INR360 crores committed (about 90% of project cost); target commissioning Q3 FY27. Guided utilisation about 20% in Q4 FY27, about 95% in FY28, and 90-100% thereafter. Contract price around $7/kg on formula basis, with spot-linked sales for about 35% of volume.

segments.name: New fluorinated inorganic products
segments.commentary: Several new products added in early commercialisation with subdued margins and lower introductory pricing for penetration; management expects their share of H2 volume to rise significantly.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth revised to 35-40% from earlier 30% guidance; FY28 revenue growth guided at 55-60%.
EBITDA margin: H2 FY27 about 18%, full FY27 average about 16%, FY28 about 24-26% with full-year HFC-32 production; separately stated H2 margin range of 15-17% from H2 onwards.
HFC-32 commissioning Q3 FY27, with revenue contribution from Q4 FY27; FY27 HFC-32 volumes estimated at 2,000-3,000 MT.
FY27 total capex about INR440-450 crores, with INR70-80 crores balance remaining in FY27; FY28 minimum capex about INR250 crores for AHF and solar grade expansion.
Expected sulphur price moderation and fluorspar inventory normalisation to 3-4 months within 1-2 quarters; receivable days expected to fall about 15 days from next quarter.
capex_capacity: HFC-32 plant: INR395 crores project, about INR360 crores incurred by September 2026; funded by INR350 crores equity (INR250 crores QIP plus INR100 crores preferential) and about INR50 crores debt.
AHF capacity planned to rise from 30,000 MT to 45,000 MT (third plant, 15,000 MT), without cannibalising external sales.
Solar grade DHF capacity planned to double from 25,000 MT to 50,000 MT in a next expansion; new solar-grade capex estimated at INR90-100 crores per new entrant.
Unutilised issue proceeds of INR157 crores, mainly committed to ongoing projects and expected to be used by end of FY27.
Medium-term greenfield plans for electronic chemicals, fluoropolymers and next-generation gases; priority decision expected in 3-4 months, with a forward-integration announcement possibly in January.
demand_pricing: Solar grade DHF demand cited rising from about 25,000 MT to about 1 lakh MT as Indian solar cell capacity grows from 30 GW to about 100 GW in three years; management sees no near-term competition given capex and about one-year gestation.

R-32 contract price rose from about $5.5/kg to about $7/kg on formula basis; spot prices expected at $6.7-7+ levels. Contract/spot mix about 65:35 to 60:40. Management expects FY28 realisations of $6.5-7.5/kg if raw material costs normalise.
Sulphur prices rose about 5x over a year (about INR25/kg in Nov 2025 to about INR120/kg in Sep 2026), now stable to slightly declining. Management cited 10-15% cost increase across the board.
Q2 revenue growth attributed about 85-87% to realisation and 12-15% to volume; management said volumes grew at least 15% YoY.
Chinese R-32 prices elevated, Indian prices lower, so import activity is minimal; 40,000 MT of new Indian R-32 capacity cited as coming in December.
Fluorspar accounts for about 70% of raw material value; inventory raised to 6-7 months after bulk procurement amid West Asia supply risk.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross and EBITDA margins fall sharply, and how will H2 and FY28 look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross profit per ton was stable and the percentage drop reflects higher realisations. Expected H2 FY27 EBITDA margin about 18%, FY27 about 16%, and FY28 about 24-26% with full-year HFC-32.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 45-day lag in passing on raw material costs the cause of the margin dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, for solar grade DHF the pass-through lag is about 45 days, while newly introduced products carry lower introductory pricing. Management expects both to benefit as sulphur prices stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital days rise from 91 to 104?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days rose from 57 to 72 because September was a major billing month; about 70% was collected in October. Inventory rose to 64 days (fluorspar buffer), offset by payables rising to 33 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR50 crore debt-funded portion and remaining capex be sufficient?
qa_highlights.answer: Funding is about INR350 crores equity and about INR50 crores debt for the INR395 crore HFC-32 project. Total FY27 capex is about INR440-450 crores, with INR250 crores minimum for FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue growth split and AHF capacity headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 growth of 37% split about 85-87% realisation and 12-15% volume. Of the 31,000-32,000 MT AHF output, about 12,000 MT goes to solar grade and 13,000 MT to R-32, leaving 3,000-5,000 MT for existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue from Anupam Rasayan (parent) in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 revenue from the parent was INR2-3 crores, which is not significant.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on sulphur and fluorspar price stabilisation and the 30-45 day pass-through lag; H1 gross margin 32.5% vs 39% last year.
HFC-32 commissioning slippage risk for Q3 FY27; FY27 ramp-up volumes of only 2,000-3,000 MT and 20% utilisation in Q4 are assumed.
Working capital intensity: inventory at 6-7 months of fluorspar, receivable days at 72, and payable build-up that management expects to normalise in 1-2 quarters.
Solar grade expansion (25,000 to 50,000 MT) and a new AHF plant are unannounced, and no back-to-back offtake contract is yet executed for the 5,000 MT debottlenecked volume.
R-32 pricing exposure: about 35% of volume is uncontracted at spot; new Indian R-32 capacity in December could weigh on prices.
Reported ROE fell sharply after equity infusion; adjusted ROE about 18% excluding issue proceeds.

506879|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.1% YoY to INR43.8 crore and EBITDA margin hit 47.5%, while the company pursues a debt- and equity-funded acquisition of MicroBiopharm Japan and Sanofi brands.
506879|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR43.8 crore (up 22.1% YoY) on higher sales volumes, with EBITDA up 49.4% to INR20.8 crore at a 47.5% margin and PAT of INR11.1 crore (up 22.1%). Management described the business as sold out in capacity for years and said the expanded fermentation capacity (about 540 KL, roughly doubling capacity) starts full operation by end-August 2026. The call focused mostly on the strategic pivot to a fermentation-based CDMO, the MicroBiopharm Japan (MBJ) acquisition, and the Sanofi brand portfolio, with funding (up to INR1,000 crore equity, debt mix undecided) and deal timing left open.

segments.name: Standalone GTBL - fermentation and API (Rifamycin-S, Rifapentine, Rifaximin)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue has been stuck around the historic INR40 crore run rate; API block bookings are in Rifapentine, Rifaximin and Rifamycin-S. Management said API output began only recently because intermediate capacity was the constraint.

segments.name: MicroBiopharm Japan (MBJ) - to be acquired
segments.commentary: MBJ is about 100% API CDMO, with roughly 4-5% formulations; 60% of its business is CDMO, and revenue is 60% Japan and 40% outside Japan. Revenue by vertical was not disclosed. ADCs are patented but have no CDMO project yet; other platforms are commercialised.

segments.name: Sanofi brands (13 anti-TB and anti-infective brands)
segments.commentary: Branded generics sold in 55 countries across Europe, Middle East and Africa. Revenue and margin figures were not disclosed. Manufacturing will move to CMOs over a 3-year transition services agreement.

Hybrid power Phase 1 expected to go live in September 2026, Phase 2 about two months later; management expects EBITDA margin improvement.
Management expects some synergy projects with MBJ within the first year.

Hybrid power project is in progress and expected to lower power costs.

Rifampicin to Rifapentine market shift is slower than hoped; management said Rifa-S demand is unaffected because GTBL is ready with both APIs.
A dispute with Optimus Drugs, a major customer, has been resolved and business is restarting; management said other buyers were available and capacity was sold out during the suspension.
Management said the company aims to sell intermediates to other Indian and global API makers to reduce customer concentration.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there nearly a three-year gap in earnings calls, and why was the API block revenue delayed from FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business was flat but sold out; capex was late by about a year. API could not start because intermediate capacity was fully contracted to long-term customers.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR3,000 crore acquisition make sense given interest costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Sanofi deal is expected to close later, with long-stop June 2027, and that interest rates in the target geographies are much lower than 10%. It said the business is cash-flow positive from the start.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding structure for the MBJ and Sanofi deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity raise of up to INR1,000 crore is planned; the debt component is undecided and will depend on the optimal mix, with options kept open.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for the base business in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR10-15 crore of last-mile capex remains, and total base-business capex including maintenance is about INR20 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path from Sanofi brands to manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: A 3-year transition services agreement will move marketing authorisations country by country, with manufacturing moved to CMOs; management hopes for faster transfer, with tech transfer complete in year 1.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Themis Medicare merger withdrawn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an external strategy review led it to focus on a fermentation-based CDMO and avoid diluting focus with predominantly domestic businesses.
