507205|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 net revenue rose 148% YoY to INR 949 crore and EBITDA margin was 16.3%, with Imperial Blue consolidated; FY27 guided to 16-18% combined EBITDA margin.
507205|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 volumes rose 135% YoY to over 8 million cases, of which Imperial Blue (IB) contributed 4.6 million cases, while ex-IB volumes were roughly flat as Andhra Pradesh base effects reversed. Reported net revenue was INR 949 crore (INR 941 crore subsidy-adjusted) and EBITDA was INR 155 crore at a 16.3% margin, or INR 146 crore and 15.5% subsidy-adjusted. Management changed presentation so trade discounts and schemes are netted from gross revenue, which lowers reported revenue and gross margin but lifts EBITDA and PAT margins without changing absolute figures. FY27 guidance covers high-single to low-double digit volume growth and a 16-18% combined EBITDA margin over 24-36 months.

financial_highlights.change: +5.4% vs INR 1,116 in Q4 FY25; ex-IB NSR +2.6%
Mainly TSMA fees and labour code impact

segments.name: Imperial Blue (IB)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume of 4.6 million cases; ex-Maharashtra growth about 9% YoY. H2 is about 52% of IB volumes. Management does not disclose brand-wise NSR; IB NSR is said to be about INR 20-30 above combined NSR under the new presentation.

segments.name: Ex-IB base business (TI)
segments.commentary: Ex-IB volumes were flat in Q4 against a high Andhra Pradesh base from the route-to-market change in Oct/Nov 2024; secondary sales grew about 5%. FY26 ex-IB volume was 13.6 million cases, up 14%.

segments.name: Mansion House brandy
segments.commentary: Crossed 10 million cases in FY26 and is India's largest P&A brandy. TI holds close to 40% P&A IMFL share in Southern India in Q4 FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth of high-single digit to low-double digit for the combined business, then double-digit volume growth over the next couple of years; double-digit volume CAGR over 3 years.
Combined EBITDA margin of 16-18% over the next 24-36 months, with 15.5% FY26 as the base; the lower end implies about 50 bps improvement.
Net debt to EBITDA below 1.0x by FY29; net debt of about INR 1,700 crore by March 2027.
Capex about INR 25 crore each in FY27 and FY28, maintenance only.
TSMA fees to decline quarter on quarter, with a full-year FY27 impact of INR 55-60 crore; all TSMA states to transition by March 2027.
Working capital cycle of 53-55 days of gross revenue on an ongoing basis.
Combined-business margin benefit of 60-100 bps from the India-UK FTA scotch duty cut, mostly on IB; Telangana price increase is possible but timing is unknown.
Q1 FY27 margins expected to see some short-term pressure from input cost inflation.
capex_capacity: Prag (Andhra Pradesh) bottling capacity raised from 6 lakh to 36 lakh cases per annum after government approval; investment about INR 59 crore, fully spent; bottling savings of about INR 10 crore per year expected.
Nigeria subsidiary investment of up to INR 30 crore; existing business about 2.5 lakh cases.
Shrirampur ENA distillery was under qualification issues; recommissioning investment is under consideration with no timing set.
Capex of about INR 25 crore a year in FY27-FY28, maintenance only.
demand_pricing: Karnataka excise policy cut consumer prices of Imperial Blue and Mansion House by about INR 20 per 180 ml nip; previous Karnataka cut (INR 257 to INR 235 per nip) drove growth there above high teens.
Telangana dues stable in days since January; management is working with the government to reduce outstanding days.
Brandy P&A (prestige and above) expected to grow at a similar clip to TI's overall growth; northern brandy launch planned in FY27.
Selling expenses under the new presentation are about 6-6.5% of grossed-up revenue, per management.
Amara Vodka (SSL portfolio) expected to gain traction from the usership arrangement.

Q4 FY26 NSR up 5.4% to INR 1,177 per case; a Karan Kamdar estimate of IB at about INR 2,400 crore annualised revenue was described as directionally right with the NSR adjusted for the accounting change.

qa_highlights.question: Why was ex-IB volume flat in Q4, and what is IB seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY25 Andhra Pradesh sales were inflated by the route-to-market change; secondary ex-IB growth was about 5%. IB is fairly evenly spread across quarters, with H2 about 52% of volume.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 250-400 bps margin expansion comes from the India-UK FTA duty cut versus operational initiatives?
qa_highlights.answer: The duty cut is worth 60-100 bps on the combined business, mostly on IB. The rest comes from cost optimisation and possible price increases, including Telangana.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IB run rate and the growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: IB growth should be similar to or slightly above the combined business because of its lower FY26 base; Maharashtra impact is largely in the FY26 base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 IB NSR?
qa_highlights.answer: Brand-wise NSR is not disclosed. Under the new net-of-selling-expense presentation, IB NSR is about INR 20-30 above the combined NSR.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no gross debt guidance, and what is net debt at March 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is less relevant because of a 2-year moratorium; net debt is expected at about INR 1,700 crore by March 2027, with upside bias.

qa_highlights.question: What are the margin path and the Q1 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management uses 15.5% as the base. The full year should hold the guided range, but Q1 FY27 faces input cost inflation, so no Q1 expansion is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Will TSMA costs keep hitting operating expenses after transition?
qa_highlights.answer: No. TSMA is treated as an exceptional item, and only about 5% of the cost is expected to recur in operating expenses.

507205|2026-06.headline: Tilaknagar Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 166% YoY to Rs 1,046 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 16.1% amid packaging inflation.
507205|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter with Imperial Blue (IB) inside the combined business, with volumes up 172% YoY and 9% QoQ, led by IB at 5.4 million cases (+18% QoQ). NSR rose to Rs 1,183 per case (+1.5% QoQ, +5.3% YoY), but glass-led packaging inflation compressed gross margin to 42.1% (adjusted for subsidy) from 45.2% in Q4 FY26. Adjusted-for-subsidy EBITDA was Rs 148 crore at 14.5%, and net debt rose to Rs 2,100 crore on working-capital build. Management reiterated FY27 volume guidance and a net debt target of about Rs 1,700 crore by March 2027.

segments.commentary: Volume grew 7% YoY in Q1 despite April disruptions.

Beyond FY27: annual volume growth in mid-teens over the next couple of years; revenue growth at least ~300 bps above volume growth; new launches from FY28 onwards.

qa_highlights.answer: Management reported good volume uptake and significantly improved operating-segment market share since the price reduction.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said segment activity is rising after years of inactivity by leaders; company is increasing A&SP reinvestment and activating in 28,000+ outlets.

qa_highlights.question: Margin recovery timing to 15.5% and beyond?

507205|2026-09.headline: Tilaknagar Q2 FY27 net revenue Rs 1,035 crore (+173% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 148 crore (14.3% margin), with inflation cutting margin about 2.5 points.

Glass packaging and emerging ENA inflation pressured gross margin, which was 41.8% adjusted for subsidy versus 42.1% in Q1. Management maintained FY27 and FY29 guidance, citing Tamil Nadu regulatory reform, Karnataka recovery, and a price-mix lift of about 200 bps from future state price increases. Net debt eased slightly from June to Rs 2,074 crore.

507514|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue fell 14.8% to INR1,233 crore and EBITDA to INR89.7 crore after the Bhopal licence suspension; FY27 guided at INR1,400-1,500 crore.
507514|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: consolidated revenue fell 14.8% to INR1,233 crore, EBITDA declined to INR89.7 crore and PAT was INR10.2 crore. Beer volumes dropped 20% to 187.19 lakh cases, driven by the temporary licence suspension at the Bhopal plant and weak demand in Karnataka and Odisha, while IMFL grew 32% to 15.03 lakh cases. Management said the Bhopal licence renewal is pending with authorities, with no definite timeline; the UP greenfield brewery has begun trials and commercial production is expected from June 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR1,400-1,500 crore and FY27 EBITDA margin to close to 10%, with FY28 guidance deferred about six months.

segments.name: Beer
segments.commentary: Volumes fell 20% to 187.19 lakh cases in FY26 due to the Bhopal licence disruption and weak Karnataka and Odisha demand. Management said Karnataka is improving after excise rationalisation, and April-May industry growth was about 15-16%.

segments.name: IMFL / premium spirits
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 32% to 15.03 lakh cases in FY26, led by premium portfolio penetration. Mahavat Whisky was launched in the mid-premium segment, and supply was halted when Bhopal stopped.

segments.name: Bhopal plant
segments.commentary: Management said roughly 50% of company volume historically came from Bhopal. Production has been halted since February and Delhi, UP and Jharkhand supplies from this plant stopped; finished goods were cleared and sold.

segments.name: UP greenfield brewery (subsidiary SDBL)
segments.commentary: About INR250 crore invested in FY26. Capacity is 1 crore cases per annum, with 15-20 lakh cases targeted in FY27 at about INR600 per case, roughly INR120 crore revenue at that realisation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guided at INR1,400-1,500 crore (management called INR1,440-1,450 crore quite possible), assuming Bhopal resumes operations.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at close to 10%; FY28 guidance to be given in about six months due to inflation in glass bottles, cans and barley.
Q1 FY27 results expected to be better than Q4 FY26, helped by better utilisation at Hassan and Odisha and some one-off annual costs in Q4 not recurring.
Management expects Bhopal market share to return to earlier levels about six to seven months after the plant restarts.
UP plant expected to start commercial production in June 2026; full capacity ramp-up expected to take 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Bhopal plant licence renewal is underway; management said it could be resolved in a couple of weeks, but later said a resolution could come within 7-10 days and gave no definite date.
UP brewery (1 crore cases per annum): trials under way, commercial operations expected from June 2026; Phase 1 is the brewery and no further capex is needed beyond working capital.
About INR400 crore of credit lines sanctioned but not drawn, which management will use only after Bhopal is operational.
Possible Phase 2 of the UP project could be the use of new promoter or warrant funds; no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Karnataka (about 30-35% of business) is improving after the state's excise duty rationalisation, which lowered MRP on mainstream and economy beer; management says it is gaining share over the last 3-4 quarters.
Industry volume in April and May 2026 grew about 15-16% combined, with April at 51-52 lakh cases and May at about 50 lakh cases despite rain.
Delhi, Jharkhand and UP supplies from Bhopal have stopped; Jharkhand is partly served from Odisha, while some markets are not cost-effective to serve from other plants.
Andhra Pradesh business expected to start in the next 3-4 weeks; Tamil Nadu share is growing.
Input cost inflation in glass bottles, aluminium cans, barley and logistics is the main margin pressure; long-term supply contracts are not holding price.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA margin outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue guided at INR1,400-1,500 crore, with the Bhopal licence assumed. FY27 EBITDA margin close to 10%; FY28 guidance deferred about six months.

qa_highlights.question: How much will the UP plant contribute in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: 15-20 lakh cases from UP in FY27 at roughly INR600 per case, about INR120 crore; plant capacity is 1 crore cases per annum with a 2-3 year ramp-up.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 FY27 going to be as loss-making as Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management expects Q1 to be better than Q4 on higher Hassan and Odisha utilisation and lower annual costs booked in Q4. Only labour cost at Bhopal will fall; no salary cuts were made.

qa_highlights.question: How long to regain Bhopal and MP market share once the plant reopens?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to recover the similar market share within about six months, though the main season makes it harder now. Management said the sales and distribution team is ready and waiting.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a one-time impact from Karnataka's excise cut?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-time impact. The MRP cut lowers consumer prices; management said revenue would rise slightly and margins would not suffer.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the licence lost and what internal steps are being taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some matters are sub judice and cannot be discussed. It is appointing a dedicated compliance officer and improving compliance processes. The company said the rating downgrades stem only from the licence suspension.

risks_watch: Bhopal licence renewal timing is open-ended. Management's timelines have slipped from days to weeks to months, and the FY27 guidance depends on it.
Input cost inflation (glass, cans, barley) with no fixed-price contracts; FY28 margin guidance deferred.
Credit rating downgrades at parent and subsidiary; management says ratings will recover once the licence is restored. About INR400 crore of undrawn lines are available.
Governance: the Company Secretary resigned (personal reasons, per management) and an internal auditor left; a compliance officer is being appointed.
Market share loss in MP and Delhi may not be fully recovered, per management's own comments.

Consolidated volume was 45.79 lakh cases, total income INR268.8 crore and EBITDA INR15.2 crore. Karnataka (cases up about 30%) and Odisha (up about 40%) recovered, and the UP brewery (about 10 million cases capacity) began commercial production around June 9, 2026. Gross debt rose only INR10 crore QoQ, with gross D/E moving from 0.3x to 0.31x, and operating cash generation was about INR28 crore. FY27 revenue guidance was lowered to INR1,000-1,100 crore from the earlier INR1,400-1,500 crore.

507526|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 net revenue INR239 crores, EBITDA up 13% to INR40 crores at 17% margin; proprietary IMFL volumes up 37% YoY.
507526|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 net revenue was INR239 crores, with EBITDA up 13% YoY to INR40 crores (17% margin, up 200 bps) and PAT up 5% to INR24 crores (10% margin). Proprietary IMFL, the main growth driver, posted 37% volume growth and a record 22% segment EBITDA margin, while the Inbrew shift from licensing to contract manufacturing kept FY26 top-line growth flattish. Ethanol volumes fell 35% YoY on industry oversupply, and merchant ENA volumes rose 129%. Management guided to FY27 EBITDA margin of around 15% and double-digit consolidated revenue growth, and announced the acquisition of SDF Industries, a Kerala distillery-cum-bottling unit.

qa_highlights.answer: Decline attributed to industry oversupply and lower allocation. Management is pursuing OMCs plus private oil companies and expects volume recovery if blending rises from 20% to 22-25%.

qa_highlights.answer: Main impact is higher packaging costs, not consumption; transport costs may rise if petrol prices rise. FY27 EBITDA guidance is about 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ethanol loss-making at EBIT and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ethanol is a non-core, economies-of-scale play with about 7% EBITDA for the year; strategy is to run the plant efficiently, add buyers and improve procurement. Management did not directly dispute the segment EBIT loss.

507526|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 IMFL proprietary volume rose 40% YoY to 0.79 million cases, with revenue up 58% to INR792 million, while consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 11% on ethanol weakness.
507526|2026-06.overview: Consolidated income from operations was INR2,809 million (+5% YoY), EBITDA INR299 million at 11% margin, and PAT INR178 million (6% margin). The proprietary IMFL brands drove growth, with the CP series volume up 260% YoY and proprietary share of revenue rising to 23% from 17%. Margins compressed mainly from ethanol, where realisations fell on oversupply and lower government quota, and from higher grain prices. Management reiterated about 30% IMFL proprietary volume growth for FY27 and flagged the SDF Kerala bottling plant moving to full operation from April 2027.

Frozen food is the growth engine: about USD3 million in Q1 (up ~20%) and USD12 million last year, with a target of USD30-plus million in three years. 507552|2026-09.headline: Foods & Inns posted a forex loss of INR106 million in Q2 FY27 from forward contracts, with ~3,300 MT unshipped orders expected to clear in Q3.

Management said there are no cancellations, only deferrals, and expects all carry-over execution in Q3. The company has stopped booking new forward covers since April and is discussing possible bank penalties.

507717|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 483.34 crore vs Rs 442.02 crore (about 9% growth), with EBITDA of Rs 124.89 crore vs Rs 109.75 crore and PAT of Rs 97.77 crore vs Rs 75.50 crore. Management attributed the record EBITDA margin largely to a sharp rise in GST refund income in Q4 (Rs 14.5 crore of the Rs 29 crore full-year refund), and said Q4 value and volume growth were roughly equal. Management guided FY27 to low double-digit growth, with the Bayer-acquired molecules (India plus rest of world) and biostimulant recovery as the main offsets to the loss of GST refund and biostimulant disruption. Input costs rose 3-5% at basket level in March-April, with pass-through expected to be gradual and largely complete by Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the guidance breakdown for FY27?

507717|2026-06.headline: Dhanuka Q1 FY27 revenue fell 12.56% YoY to Rs 461.93 crore; EBITDA Rs 55.01 crore and PAT Rs 36.30 crore, with FY27 growth guided to small single digits.
507717|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined about 12.56% YoY to Rs 461.93 crore from Rs 528.29 crore, with volume down about 12.7% and value down 12.56%, per management. Management attributed the quarter to delayed monsoon onset, a June rainfall deficit of about 40% (narrowing to 15% by end-July), weak herbicide demand in soybean and cotton states, and price erosion after a short-lived price hike. Management now expects a small single-digit growth in FY27 crop protection, versus the earlier guidance that was cut in the presentation. Biologicals, Bayer-acquired molecules and the Nagpur formulation plant (Rs 200 crore outlay, 23,000 MT) are the main forward-looking items.

qa_highlights.question: Why such a steep guidance cut, especially on top-line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is giving a realistic picture given monsoon movement; still hopeful of Q2 and Q3 growth, and the outlook was reset to small single-digit growth for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 200 crore Nagpur capex high for a formulation plant?

507717|2026-09.headline: Dhanuka Q2 FY27 revenue rose 9.91% to INR657.51 crore, but management reiterated only a low-single-digit full-year growth and ~100 bps gross margin loss.
507717|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew about 9.9% YoY to INR657.51 crore, with EBITDA of INR152.97 crore and PAT of INR109.22 crore, both up YoY. Growth was driven by insecticides (47% of revenue), which management attributed to El Niño-led product focus and channel agility rather than market share gains. Management said Q2 growth is not a run-rate: it expects low single-digit revenue growth for the full year, with Q3 and Q4 subdued and gross margin down about 100 bps. Analysts probed channel inventory, margin drivers, Dahej plant ramp-up and the new-product index, and management was specific on most points but declined product-level revenue figures.

segments.name: Zones (share of Q2 turnover)
segments.commentary: North 31%, East 12%, West 28%, South 29%. Analyst noted North grew about 22% in Q2 and about 12% in H1; management attributed North strength to irrigated markets.

segments.name: Product categories (share of Q2 revenue)
segments.commentary: Insecticides 47%, fungicides 25%, herbicides 8%, others 20%. Herbicides were hit by dry weather; insecticides grew strongly.

segments.name: Dahej (Harsh Dhanuka)

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 revenue growth now guided at low single digit (management clarified this after earlier single-digit guidance; a Q2 growth of about 10% is not a run-rate for Q3 and Q4).
Gross margin expected to fall about 100 bps for the year, with EBITDA decline similar or slightly larger; management said margin expansion will not happen this year.
Q3 and Q4 described as subdued; management does not expect a high sales season in Q3.
Rabi season initial movement described as promising in certain regions; South and East zones are the key for Rabi.
Management said the GST refund effect on gross margin recurs every quarter; excluding it, gross margin is flat.

Two plant growth regulator and growth influencer launches planned in Q3.
capex_capacity: Dahej plant at about 70% utilisation; capacity expansion of existing products approved along with 2 new fungicide products in the existing plant (FY28).
Capex quantum not disclosed; management said clarity will come in a later round but the company is 'absolutely committed' to capex.
Two R&D centres with NABL-accredited labs; partnerships with 10 multinational agrochemical innovators from Japan, Europe and the US.
Distribution footprint: over 10 million farmers reached via 6,500 distributors, 80,000-plus retailers and 40-plus warehouses.
demand_pricing: Q2 growth attributed to insecticides (LaNevo, Miyako, Mortar, Decis), plant growth regulators and nutritional products; management said this was product-specific, not market share gain.
Chilli in South and cotton (repeat insecticide sprays) and vegetables in East supported demand; fungicide demand was weak.

Generic crop pricing under severe pressure; management said tepid demand prevents full pass-through of raw material cost increases. Some raw materials fell in Q2 and others rose; increases passed on selectively.

Channel inventory described as optimal; company said it cleans channel monthly and did not front-load in Q1. Analyst asked about receivables jump; management said debtors are not aggressively placed and material is taken back quickly.

Polin (paddy fungicide from Nippon Soda, Japan) priced above market acceptance; not expected to scale near term.
Brazil and European subsidiaries are for registration only; customers appointed in about 14 countries, purchase orders in hand from 5.

qa_highlights.question: What drove about 10% growth in Q2 and was there regional share gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was product-specific insecticide growth from El Niño-driven re-planning, plus focus on water-available areas and no Q1 channel front-loading. Q2 growth is not an indicator for the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10% growth a run-rate, and will growth moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained single-digit growth guidance for the year, saying Q2 growth reflects the weak base of last year's same quarter and is not indicative of Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong North performance (about 22% in Q2) market share gain or industry-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said North irrigated markets (Punjab, Haryana, Western UP) were industry's favourite; it would not confirm share gain.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin held despite lowest ITI and high-margin mix moderation: what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said gross margin was slightly lower YoY due to GST refund effects; EBITDA margin improved mainly from tighter other expenses. Value growth (10%) exceeded volume growth (6%).

qa_highlights.question: Full-year guidance: high single digit or double digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Dhanuka said the company will grow by a single low digit for the year, with gross margin down about 100 bps and EBITDA down similarly or slightly more.

qa_highlights.question: Will product-level revenue such as LaNevo be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share product-specific revenue, though it said LaNevo was a leading growth driver in Q2.

risks_watch: Full-year guidance cut to low single-digit growth; Q3 and Q4 subdued, with weak demand in the Western and Central regions where rain opportunity has ended.
Gross margin pressure of about 100 bps; competitors' high-cost inventory could pressure generic pricing in H2.
Dahej remains loss-making; capex quantum and timelines for the two new fungicides not yet disclosed.
Enforcement against unregistered and spurious products; industry-wide concern flagged, with FICCI involvement.
Rabi season performance in South and East zones is the key swing factor.
New-product index (ITI) moderation; Polin unlikely to scale near term, pipeline depends on Q3 PGR launches and Dhanzyme Gold December launch.

507779|2026-06.headline: Kanpur Plastipack Q1 FY27 standalone total income Rs 207.49 cr (first time above Rs 200 cr) and PAT up 112% YoY to Rs 12.14 cr, with EBITDA margin at 10.69%.

FIBC volume fell to about 3,000 tonnes from 3,500 tonnes a year earlier, due to polymer and labour disruptions. The premium polypropylene Taslan yarn JV with Essegomma (Italy) started commercial production and sales, with volume ramp guided from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Shubhi Gupta (Trinetra Asset Managers): How is raw material volatility from the West Asia conflict progressing, and can raw material moves be passed to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Polymer volatility has eased from about plus/minus 25% in March to plus/minus 10% now. Raw material changes are generally passed through with a lag of two weeks to one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Shubhi Gupta: What is the marginal differential and expected EBITDA from the B2C-linked premium segments, and what total EBITDA margin should be expected for the company?
qa_highlights.answer: ESSEKAN is expected to add about Rs 10 crore revenue in FY27 at 20-25% EBITDA; non-woven B2C is guided to mid-double-digit EBITDA. Management would not give an exact company-wide margin guide but expects to sustain current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor (Kapoor & Co): What is ESSEKAN's peak revenue on current capacity and when would more capacity be added?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity can reach about Rs 30 crore revenue. More capacity will be added once utilisation hits 50-60%, as the capex is not high.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: Why did margins not expand more despite the 31% ASP rise versus 18% raw material rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing EBITDA margin was 12.6%. Employee cost rose about Rs 3-3.5 crore QoQ, FIBC manufactured volume fell due to supply chain and labour disruptions, and there were packing, oil, freight and one-time disruption costs. Energy costs were not a significant increase.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What are the factors ahead for the rest of the year, and what are the FIBC capacity and mix plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Two risks: ocean freight rising from about $2,000 to $5,000 per container could dent demand, and partial sharing of costs with customers could hit margins. Target is 5,000 tonnes per quarter by Q1 FY28; management declined to give a product mix percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What was the FIBC utilisation and is 3,000 tonnes the base for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes were 3,800 tonnes in Q3 FY26, 3,500 in Q4 FY26 and 3,000 in Q1 FY27, with working-day seasonality. Management called 3,000 a damaged number that will build from here.

qa_highlights.question: Chaitrika (individual investor): What is the long-term revenue aspiration and what are the milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Current projects and installed capacity can take revenue to about Rs 900-950 crore in FY27-28 and Rs 1,000-1,050 crore in FY29, assuming current trading and polymer prices. Management will decide on deploying balance-sheet cash for further capacity next year.

qa_highlights.question: Yash Parker (individual investor): What tangible benefits have the UK (Valex) and Italian JV delivered, and when will financials show?
qa_highlights.answer: ESSEKAN sampling is under way with significant commercialisation expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27, with guidance on it by Q4. Valex has delivered no significant tangible benefit so far beyond brand awareness; its turnover is manufacturing-transferred, so profit sits within Kanpur Plastipack.

qa_highlights.question: Yash Parker: What annual savings come from renewable power, and what is the FIBC capacity ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewable power is about 60% of energy and already at the planned level, saving about Rs 3-5 crore a year. Battery storage is a couple of years away. FIBC adds about 1,200 tonnes a year, so 4-5 years to reach the full 6,000 tonnes.

qa_highlights.question: Yash Parker: What IRR and ROCE hurdles apply, and what working capital is needed as the business ramps?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-woven targets 15-20% IRR and ROCE above 20%; ESSEKAN returns are far higher given low capex. Working capital stays at similar levels for FIBC and raffia, while non-woven adds 30-40 days of working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Deeya Jain (Sapphire Capital): What are the realisation trends, and the ESSEKAN revenue targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisations track raw material and freight costs and should hold while raw material costs are steady. ESSEKAN is about Rs 10 crore in FY27, with an ultimate aim of Rs 100 crore in four years.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What is the impairment, contract value and debt position?

rows.why: Asset-light model with no manufacturing capacity disclosed and no manpower addition beyond budget; backend manufacturing is under evaluation with no decision yet.

507815|2026-03.headline: Gillette India FY26 sales rose 8% to ₹3,100 crore and PAT rose 23% to about ₹650 crore, with the company citing a ~300bps structural margin gain.
507815|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) sales of about ₹3,100 crore, up 8%, and PAT of about ₹650 crore, up 23%, attributed to productivity across cost buckets. Management said the topline slowdown was largely due to one-time export impacts from affiliate distribution changes, including the Bangladesh distribution agreement closure, and that domestic sales were growing quarter on quarter. The call focused on new launches (Gillette Guard 3in1, Gillette trimmers, Oral-B Sensitive), Venus growth, productivity, and raw material inflation linked to the West Asia conflict. Management gave no numerical FY27 guidance.

segments.name: Male grooming (Blades and Razors)
segments.commentary: Management says the category grows about 12% and Gillette remains market leader; male grooming offtake grew 8% in P6M and 12% in P12M. Gillette Guard grew double digit and premium razors grew in early teens.

segments.name: Female grooming (Venus)
segments.commentary: Venus contributes double digits to grooming and is growing upwards of 20%; female grooming overall is growing upwards of 20%. The focus is new-user growth in in-home hair removal.

segments.name: Manual oral care (Oral-B)
segments.commentary: Growing high single digits, driven by the Oral-B Sensitive range, which is growing double digit and is among the fastest growing segments in the category.

segments.name: Power oral care (Oral-B)
segments.commentary: Growing at roughly 1.5x this year and at double digits steadily; business has doubled in the last 3 years.

segments.name: Trimmers and appliances
segments.commentary: Four new Gillette trimmers launched about 2 months before the call; management expects the trimmers category to grow at early double digits.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 sales or margin guidance was given; management said it expects some challenges to continue in the near term.
Management aims to grow ahead of the male grooming category and keep balancing topline and bottom-line growth.
A multi-year savings and productivity plan is in place by business unit to support margins and offset input-cost inflation.
Management said it cannot comment on future margins but expects productivity to fund investment and provide cover against macro volatility.
Management expects growth may fluctuate in the mid-term; it sees India growing at 6.5% for the year.
capex_capacity: About 85% of products are manufactured domestically; finished goods are exported to more than 10 countries.
Bhiwadi manufacturing plant issue was resolved within a few days with zero supply-related shortfall, per management.
Management is constantly assessing the locally manufactured vs imported supply chain mix.
Supply 3.0 advance ordering now covers half of the business; over 2 million automated on-shelf availability checks are run daily.
demand_pricing: Gillette Guard 3in1 (launched about 2 months earlier): about 1 million razors sold in the launch month, distribution reached over 6 lakh stores, and a new copy reached 20 crore viewers in month 1.
Numeric distribution rose by a couple of points in FY26 for priority SKUs; premium Mach3 and Fusion distribution grew at mid-single digits for 3 years.
Gillette Guard added 20 million new users over the last 3 years.
Management said raw material costs were hit by crude up ~50% and resins up ~50%, with availability challenged; the company said it did not go out of stock.
Management said rural consumption remains higher than urban, but rural is softening because of inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue growth subdued and volatile in FY26 and the March quarter, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one-time export impacts from affiliate-company decisions, including the Bangladesh distribution agreement closure, weigh on the base. Excluding them, growth would roughly double, and domestic sales are growing quarter on quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY26 margin gains sustainable, and what about FY27 margins and raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said structural margins improved upwards of 300 bps through premium innovation and productivity. It would not comment on FY27 but said a multi-year savings plan is in place and it will keep mitigating inflation and freight overcharges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth plan over the next 3 to 5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will double down on its five-vector integrated strategy: daily-use portfolio, superiority, productivity, constructive disruption and an enabled organisation. No numeric target was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth drivers in Venus and female grooming?
qa_highlights.answer: Venus is double digit in grooming and growing upwards of 20%; the focus is new-user growth in in-home hair removal through influencers and myth-busting content. No Venus salience figure was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the trimmers and appliances opportunity, and what share is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Four trimmers were launched about 2 months before the call; the category is expected to grow at early double digits. Management aims to grow faster than the category but gave no share target.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Bhiwadi plant issue fully resolved, and were there supply challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the issue was resolved within a few days, with zero supply-related challenges, and the stock exchange was alerted.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation: crude and resin up about 50%, with tight availability tied to West Asia conflict; the margin impact was not quantified.
Export revenue volatility from affiliate distribution changes, including the Bangladesh agreement closure.
Softening rural consumption and inflation-driven pressure on consumer spending.
Competition in men's shaving, which management acknowledged in Q&A without giving share data.
Next quarter: whether domestic growth and margin gains hold, and the early traction of Guard 3in1 and trimmers.
507815|2026-03.management_tone: Management was confident on the long-term record and category growth, but cautious on near-term challenges from inflation and supply costs. It deflected several quantitative questions (FY27 margins, share targets, Venus salience, the innovation pipeline) and said some information would be withheld as price sensitive.
key_quotes: We have consistently grown topline AND bottom-line for the last 5 years!
Gillette continues to be the market leader in the Blades and Razors segment, and we have grown year on year.
As an example, crude has been highly volatile and prices have gone up by 50%. As an outcome, resins have gone up by about 50% as well.
Despite these significant disruptions, we have not gone out of stock… or made compromises on product performance.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Structural margin gain of upwards of 300 bps in FY26 and ₹38 crore productivity savings, but management would not comment on FY27 margins and flagged crude and resin up ~50% with the margin impact unquantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Male grooming offtake grew 8% in P6M and 12% in P12M, Venus growing upwards of 20%, and Guard 3in1 sold about 1 million razors in its launch month, though FY26 sales grew only 8% and export base effects weigh.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical FY27 guidance was given and management expects some challenges to continue in the near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw material inflation (crude and resins up ~50%) and softening rural consumption could pressure growth and margins, though no quantified cut was signalled.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: already launched; traction through next 2-3 quarters
rows.why: Four new Gillette trimmers launched about 2 months before the call and Gillette Guard 3in1 launched about 2 months earlier with about 1 million razors sold in launch month.

rows.label: Input cost pass-through and freight recovery
rows.why: Management said it will keep mitigating inflation and freight overcharges under a multi-year savings plan, but gave no pricing figure and the crude and resin rise is ~50%.

rows.label: Export recovery from affiliate distribution changes
rows.why: The Bangladesh distribution agreement closure is a one-time export drag on the base; management said excluding it growth would roughly double, but the closure itself is not reversing.

rows.label: Supply 3.0 advance ordering
rows.why: Supply 3.0 advance ordering now covers half the business and over 2 million automated on-shelf checks run daily, supporting availability through the input shortage.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term record, male grooming category growth and launches, but cautious on near-term inflation, rural softening and export drag; it declined FY27 margin, share and Venus salience figures, and analysts pushed on sustainability of margins and FY27 outlook.

508814|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated sales rose 37% to Rs 1,021 crore and EBITDA rose 53% to Rs 130 crore, with net debt cut to Rs 1,159 crore.
508814|2026-03.overview: Cosmo First reported Q4 FY26 consolidated sales of Rs 1,021 crore (up 37% YoY on 41% volume growth) and EBITDA of Rs 130 crore (up 53% from Rs 85 crore), helped by new BOPP/CPP capacity, specialty volumes and a Rs 7 crore EBITDA rise at the specialty chemical subsidiary. PAT growth was moderate due to higher depreciation and interest, a Rs 7.2 crore exceptional provision at a Netherlands subsidiary and a Rs 5.3 crore deferred tax asset reversal in South Korea. For FY26, revenue rose 26% and EBITDA rose 32% to Rs 479 crore. Management said the capex cycle is largely complete, net debt fell Rs 75 crore over six months to Rs 1,159 crore, and it expects double-digit topline growth in FY27.

segments.name: BOPP/BOPET films
segments.commentary: BOPP margin about Rs 20/kg in Q4 vs Rs 13/kg in Dec-25 quarter; BOPET about Rs 18/kg vs Rs 12/kg in Dec-25 quarter. Films are about 90% BOPP-CPP and about 10% BOPET; specialty films are about 60% of films in Q4 (56-57% for full year).

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales Rs 54 crore with 25%+ EBITDA; FY26 sales Rs 204 crore. Value growth was about 10% because raw-material-linked pricing was lower, though volume grew about 20%.

segments.name: Cosmo Plastech (rigid packaging)
segments.commentary: Q4 topline up over 70% YoY; reached EBITDA breakeven in Q4 with a small PBT loss likely. FY26 turnover about Rs 92 crore. Management targets high single-digit EBITDA in FY27 and mid-to-high teens in FY28.

segments.name: Zigly (petcare)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 topline up 54% YoY; annualised run rate about Rs 90 crore. Plan to move it into a separate subsidiary in FY27, with possible external capital.

segments.name: Cosmo Consumer (window films, PPF, ceramic coatings)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 23 crore; exit annualised run rate about Rs 38 crore. Gross margin expected at 35-40%; still loss-making due to brand marketing. Management says at least two years to profitability and targets Rs 100 crore revenue first.

guidance_outlook: FY27 topline to grow in double digits, driven by utilisation of BOPP/CPP capacity added in FY26 and new businesses.
No EBITDA guidance given; management cited industry-cycle uncertainty but expects decent margins from new businesses, specialty growth and the US subsidiary.
Film volume growth potential of 15-20% from existing capacity; chemicals potential about Rs 100 crore more revenue; Plastech potential 30%; Cosmo Consumer at about 20% utilisation.
Capex for FY27 expected below Rs 100 crore; investment in Plastech, Consumer and Zigly about Rs 50-75 crore over next year and the year after.
Net debt to fall further; target to bring debt below 2x EBITDA within 12-18 months (currently 2.4x).
US tariff refund of more than Rs 60 crore expected over 6-12 months, partly payable back to customers; flows to both P&L and cash flow. Management expects Q1 FY27 to be better than Q4 FY26.
Operating cost (employee and other) expected to hold at Q4 run-rate plus inflation in FY27.
Dividend of Rs 4 per share recommended for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
risks_watch: BOPP/BOPET spreads remain volatile as 7-8 new Indian BOPP lines arrive over three years; possible short-term core-film oversupply.
Speciality pricing lag (one to three months) can compress margins during raw material price swings.
Cosmo Consumer and Plastech still loss-making at PBT level; Cosmo Consumer will keep losing money in FY27 as marketing continues.
Net debt of Rs 1,159 crore (2.4x EBITDA) and potential interest-rate pressure from inflation; deleveraging target below 2x within 12-18 months.
Timing and size of US tariff refund (above Rs 60 crore, partly payable to customers) remains uncertain.
Management gave no quantitative EBITDA guidance and called the outlook highly uncertain.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 7.2 crore provision at Netherlands subsidiary
Rs 5.3 crore, South Korea subsidiary reorganisation

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 33 crore FY25; sales Rs 204 crore, 25%+ EBITDA margin
Down Rs 75 crore in last 6 months

qa_highlights.question: What is the industry outlook for BOPP and BOPET prices and spreads in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins may stay volatile as new capacity comes, though it sees a macro demand-supply balance. It said the company controls mix and cost, specialty films are 60% of films, and it is the lowest-cost producer in India.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee and other cost base likely to keep rising after FY26 (employee expenses Rs 250 crore in FY25 vs Rs 336 crore in FY26)?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs should be held at the Q4 FY26 run rate plus normal inflation, and should fall as a percentage of sales as volumes grow.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the Plastech and Cosmo Consumer losses and when do they reach PBT break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Plastech reached EBITDA breakeven in Q4 with a possible small PBT loss; targets high single-digit EBITDA in FY27 and high-to-mid teens in FY28. Cosmo Consumer will keep losing money in FY27 due to marketing and needs at least two years to profitability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did specialty chemical growth slow to about 9-10% in FY26 against about 20% in prior years?
qa_highlights.answer: Value growth was about 10% because raw-material-linked prices were lower, while volume grew about 20%. EBITDA rose from Rs 33 crore to Rs 53 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 capacity utilisation across lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year utilisation is 80-85%, with 15-20% volume headroom in films, about Rs 100 crore revenue headroom in chemicals, 30% in Plastech and about 20% utilisation in Cosmo Consumer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt outlook and interest cost guidance amid possible rate hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt is expected to fall further, with FY27 capex below Rs 100 crore. Management aims to bring net debt/EBITDA below 2x within 12-18 months from 2.4x. It gave no interest-cost guidance.

capex_capacity: Film capacity: management cited 15-20% volume growth potential from existing BOPP/CPP capacity over last year's numbers; full-year FY26 utilisation of 80-85%.
Capex cycle described as largely complete; focus on sweating about Rs 1,200 crore of strategic capex made in the last three years.
FY27 capex expected to be below Rs 100 crore; investment in Plastech, Cosmo Consumer and Zigly about Rs 50-75 crore over the next year and the year after.
Capacity headroom in other businesses: specialty chemicals potential of about Rs 100 crore more revenue; Plastech potential growth of 30%; Cosmo Consumer at about 20% capacity utilisation.
Other businesses (Plastech, Cosmo Consumer, Zigly) have had about Rs 275-300 crore invested since inception, excluding films. Seven to eight new Indian BOPP lines expected over three years.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 BOPP margin about Rs 20/kg vs Rs 13/kg in Dec-25 quarter and Rs 20/kg in Mar-25 quarter; BOPET margin about Rs 18/kg vs Rs 12/kg in Dec-25 quarter and Rs 18/kg in Mar-25 quarter.
Management said BOPP spreads in April-May are broadly in the same range as Q4; BOPET spreads expected to rise per management trend view, with demand-supply balance in 12-18 months.
Indian flexible packaging volume growing 8-10%; BOPET demand growing 8-10% YoY with supply still slightly ahead of demand; anti-dumping duty on BOPET imports from neighbouring countries.
Specialty share of films about 60% in Q4 FY26 (down from ~70% before new BOPP line; 56-57% for full year); specialty volumes growing at about 10% CAGR.

Specialty chemicals value growth about 10% in FY26 as raw-material-linked pricing was lower, with volume growth about 20%; specialty gross margin per kg fell to Rs 63 from Rs 65 on a one-to-three-month pricing lag.
US business expected to grow at least 15-20%; US tariffs refund of more than Rs 60 crore, partly payable to customers, over 6-12 months.
Cosmo Consumer exit annualised run rate about Rs 38 crore vs FY26 revenue of Rs 23 crore; gross margin target 35-40%; management targets over 50% CAGR and Rs 100 crore revenue benchmark.
key_quotes: What we control is mix and cost.
We are also the lowest cost producer in India, which gives us downside protection.
We should see anywhere between 15 to 20% growth as a minimum in US business.
And we will bring it below within next 12 to 18 months.

rows.why: Plastech topline rose over 70% YoY and hit EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY26, and management targets high single-digit EBITDA in FY27 and mid-to-high teens in FY28.

508814|2026-06.headline: Cosmo First Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 46% to Rs 1,166 crore and EBITDA 26% to Rs 147 crore, though margin fell to 12.6%.
508814|2026-06.overview: Revenue growth was driven mainly by raw material pass-through after the West Asia conflict, with volume up only 9%. EBITDA rose 26% to Rs 147 crore, helped by better per-kg contribution across base, semi-specialty and specialty films, and management says all B2B businesses are now profitable. Export volumes fell 13% due to port congestion and a line maintenance outage, and BOPET margins compressed sharply sequentially. Net debt was flat at Rs 1,166 crore (2.3x EBITDA), and management targets below 2x within 12 months.

segments.name: BOPP films (base, semi-specialty, specialty)
segments.commentary: Specialty sales volume up 12% YoY; specialty mix at 61%, highest in five quarters, with target of 70%. Gross margin Rs 30/kg including non-repeating stock gain; management said base BOPP margin ex-stock gain was broadly flat.

segments.name: BOPET films
segments.commentary: Gross margin fell to Rs 9/kg from Rs 18/kg in Q4 FY26. Capacity is 30,000 tonnes against 277,000 tonnes of BOPP. Management expects margins to recover after recently levied anti-dumping duty.

segments.name: US film business
segments.commentary: Export volumes down 13% due to port congestion and in-transit shipments. US subsidiary received about USD 7 million duty refund in July 2026, not yet appropriated. Management expects US revenue to grow 25-30% in FY27.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue up 34% YoY with 25% EBITDA margin, improved 2 percentage points QoQ. About 80% of business is backward integration into group films. FY27 growth guided at about 50%; Rs 400-500 crore FY30 target may be reached by FY29.

segments.name: Cosmo Plastech (rigid packaging)
segments.commentary: Revenue up over 58% YoY and turned EBITDA positive. FY26 revenue about Rs 100 crore; FY27 guided Rs 150-160 crore and Rs 200+ crore next year, with capacity up 50% at minimal capex over next two quarters.

segments.name: Zigly (petcare)
segments.commentary: Monthly GMV run rate about Rs 100 crore (annualised Rs 100 crore, per the call). Gross margin 47%, services 64% of sales mix, private label revenue up 105% YoY, 47 centres, 29,000 customers in the quarter. Management estimates breakeven at about Rs 250 crore revenue, a couple of years away.

segments.name: Cosmo Consumer (window films, PPF, ceramic coatings)
segments.commentary: Near EBITDA breakeven in Q1. Revenue grew 4.5x last year and management expects more than 3x this year. Margin about 25% (EBIT per management, up from 15-17% at launch); gross margin target 35-40%. TV advertising began July 2026; 150 dealers in 100+ cities.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated topline to grow about 20% in FY27, with commensurate bottom-line growth.
New businesses to grow about 60% in FY27; specialty chemicals about 50%.
ROCE targeted at 15-20% within 12-24 months, from about 11% in the last financial year.
Net debt/EBITDA to fall below 2x within 12 months; Rs 400-500 crore debt reduction over two years with minimal capex.

India is slightly over capacity in BOPET, which management expects to correct; anti-dumping duty recently levied.
Specialty film margins above Rs 60/kg for five consecutive quarters; semi-specialty about Rs 15-20/kg above base film margins.
PPF penetration in India about 2%, growing 30%; pet care market growing 22% a year.

qa_highlights.question: How will ROCE move over the next two years given new verticals are EBITDA positive, and what are the growth levers by business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROCE was about 11% last year and is targeted at 15-20% within 12-24 months. Levers are volume growth (about 15% film capacity still to be sold), Plastech capacity +50% at minimal capex, consumer growth, and US revenue growth of 25-30% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What new BOPP specialty grades were developed, and what per-kg margin uplift do they bring?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialty sales grew 12% in the quarter; launches included synthetic paper film, PVC-free green graphic films and anti-fog BOPET lidding films. Six patents are granted and 11 are pending. Semi-specialty runs Rs 15-20/kg above base, and specialty has been above Rs 60/kg for five quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins lag revenue growth, and was the high crude-linked raw material cost passed through?

Plastech is adding 50% capacity, with revenue capacity of Rs 250+ crore, and management said specialty films can reach close to 90% without major capex.

508954|2026-09.headline: Finkurve's Q2 FY27 AUM grew about 95% YoY but only about 3% QoQ, with GNPA rising to about 2.6% and collection efficiency falling to about 90%.
508954|2026-09.overview: Management said Q2 FY27 was among its best quarters on operating profit, up 62% YoY, with AUM up about 95% YoY and branches up to 122 from 92 a year earlier. Growth slowed sharply sequentially, which management attributed to the revised RBI gold loan framework, deferred borrowing after gold price correction, and competition. Asset quality weakened: GNPA rose to about 2.6% and NNPA was 2.4%, with collection efficiency down to about 90% from about 98% in Q1, which management called a technical classification rather than a credit cost issue. Co-lending rose to about 6% of AUM, and management reiterated a target of 30-35% off-book AUM within about three years.

demand_pricing: Gold price correction from earlier-2026 highs deferred customer borrowing: customers realise less per loan amount, so they wait a quarter for prices to stabilise.

Ticket size falling due to the slab-wise LTV regime; management said it lacked data on the split and will share it after the call.
Unorganised lenders' share is falling (management cited a 60:40 to 65:35 shift) as RBI restricted repledging.

Augmont has more than 350 standard products distributed by gold loan companies, and one gold loan company sold over 28 tonnes of Augmont jewellery; Finkurve has only just started this non-interest income line.

qa_highlights.question: How will Finkurve differentiate from banks and large gold NBFCs as banks get aggressive on gold loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no product differentiation; it targets customers with little access to banks or large NBFCs, and turnaround times and scheme design are key. Yields are higher because of this segment.

508989|2026-03.headline: Navneet FY26 revenue fell 3% to INR1,683 crore; management guides FY27 publication growth of about 15% and stationery growth of about 15%, with margins to recover to around 9% after brand spend.

Domestic stationery grew 4% in value to INR366 crore on 6% volume growth, but margins were hit by GST exemption on paper stationery (blocking input tax credit) and falling paper prices passed on to customers. Management is shifting to a two-year brand-building push (about INR30 crore in FY27 and INR40-odd crore in FY28) and expects a state curriculum cycle in Maharashtra and Gujarat from FY27. Indiannica (CBSE subsidiary) posted INR42 crore sales and a INR16 crore loss, and is to be merged into Navneet.

508989|2026-09.headline: Navneet Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose about 31% to INR324 crore and standalone EBITDA rose 150% to INR20 crore, with margin at 6.2%.
508989|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue grew about 31-32% YoY from INR246 crore to INR324 crore, and standalone EBITDA rose 150% to INR20 crore (margin 3.3% to 6.2%). Standalone PAT was INR6 crore versus a loss of INR6 crore a year earlier. Publication revenue rose about 53.8% to INR140 crore, partly on Q1 spillover, while domestic and export stationery margins were pressured by brand spending, manpower, a GST reversal, new plant depreciation and export discounts given under US tariffs. Management guided to better H2 profitability and said the K12 Techno stake sale proceeds (INR330 crore received, up to INR70 crore more pending) are to be deployed after a board decision.

509079|2026-03.headline: Gufic Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 23% YoY to INR252 crore with EBITDA margin at 17.7%, while FY26 PAT fell to INR63.2 crore.
509079|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter in company history, with revenue of about INR252 crore (vs INR205 crore in Q4 FY25), EBITDA of INR44.7 crore (17.73% margin vs 13.17%) and PAT of INR20.5 crore (vs INR8 crore). Full-year revenue rose to INR940.5 crore (from INR820 crore), but EBITDA margin eased to 16.26% and PAT fell to INR63.2 crore from INR69.9 crore, reflecting Indore fixed costs, a domestic critical-care working-capital reset worth about INR22 crore of revenue, and higher overheads. Indore reached EBITDA breakeven in Q4 at about 30% capacity utilisation, as committed. Management guided to about 15% revenue growth in FY27, around 18% EBITDA margin for FY27, and gross debt held at about INR400 crore.

segments.name: Indore (CMO / complex injectables)
segments.commentary: Reached 30% capacity utilisation by year-end as targeted and EBITDA breakeven in Q4. 40 tech transfers complete, 27 under development; 200-plus state FDA approvals; more than 20 Indian pharma companies use it as CMO base. Management expects Indore margin of about 31-32% at full utilisation, with overall Indore margin around 20%.

segments.name: Navsari (existing plant)
segments.commentary: Management said Navsari margin was about 20% and expects it to settle at 18-18.5% as costs rise. Navsari is building cartridge and pen GLP-1 capabilities.

segments.name: Domestic / Critical Care
segments.commentary: About 48-50% of revenue. Hospital direct-billing receivables of 140-150+ days were reset to CFA/stockist distribution, costing about INR22 crore of revenue across Q2-Q4 FY26; collections now essentially complete. Critical care growth guided at 6-8%, maximum 9%, before new launches.

segments.name: Women's health (fertility and gynaecology)
segments.commentary: Strongest year ever. Gonadotropin flagship hit its highest annual sales; a hormone launched two years ago beat its annual target and was ranked among top new launches by IQVIA. IVF expected to grow at a decent rate, with recombinant launches planned over the next two years.

segments.name: Aesthetics (botulinum toxin and fillers)
segments.commentary: Claimed the number 2 botulinum toxin brand in India at about 23% share. Toxin is about 3.5% of revenue. A Canadian in-licensed filler is targeted for launch in Q3 or Q4 FY27, India only.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Record FY26 international business. Shifting from distributor-led model to holding marketing authorisations (Gufic Ireland for EU), with direct supply, out-licensing and tech transfer income. Exports about 20-22% of revenue. Approvals in Myanmar, Philippines, South Africa, Colombia, Germany, Ecuador in Q4; dossiers filed in 18 countries.

segments.name: CMO
segments.commentary: About 18-19% of revenue, boosted this year by GLP-1 contract work. Management guides to about 15-18% at peak. GLP-1 revenue not quantified.

segments.name: Nutraceutical and Ayurveda
segments.commentary: Focus on pain, arthritis and GI chronic therapies; a first-in-India formulation launched in heritage orthopaedic brand in Q4. No financials disclosed.

FY27 EBITDA margin around 18%, with 0.5-1% annual improvement thereafter and above 20% by FY30.

capex_capacity: Indore at about 30% utilisation at FY26-end, EBITDA breakeven in Q4; now moving to qualification, validation and tech transfer phase. Focus on complex injectables, depot, liposomal and suspensions.
EU GMP audit by Portuguese authority completed in early December 2025; certificate pending.

Management said R&D spend is about 8-10% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins, and is it operating leverage or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed gross margin gains to domestic and international reset, new launches and moving to more profitable geographies, guiding 0.5-1% YoY improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GLP-1 work a confirmed contract and how big could it be?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a CMO role with partners, too premature to quantify, and not in prior projections.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR6.5 crore invested in a cooperative bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Saraswat Bank relationship of over 15 years; investment earns about 15% dividend vs about 8% borrowing cost. Total exposure about INR250 crore across fund-based, non-fund-based and term loans. Shares can be sold back at face value.

qa_highlights.question: Size of botulinum toxin revenue and capex needs for fillers?
qa_highlights.answer: Toxin is about 3.5% (plus or minus) of revenue. The filler in-licence needs no capex, as it is imported from Canada and sold in India under the partner's brand.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance on top-line, margins and debt over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% revenue growth YoY; FY27 EBITDA about 18%; debt flat at about INR400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Indore cost sit in P&L and what is the Indore vs Navsari margin split?
qa_highlights.answer: Navsari margin about 20%, expected 18-18.5%; Indore at 31-32% at full utilisation and about 20% blended.

qa_highlights.question: How will debt and cash evolve, given the analyst's cash figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said short-term debt is enough for working capital for 2-3 years; long-term debt is falling; no debt-funded projects; growth investments funded from internal cash flow.

risks_watch: Negative FY26 PAT year-on-year despite revenue growth; FY27 margin recovery depends on Indore ramp-up and cost control.

509079|2026-06.headline: Gufic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR260.8 crore and PAT rose 86% to INR22.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 18.09%.

EBITDA rose to INR47.2 crore (18.09% margin) from INR33.2 crore (14.6%), and PAT reached INR22.46 crore (8.61% margin) versus INR12.1 crore. Management said Indore is running to plan, with capacity utilisation expected to reach 40-45% by year-end and the GLP-1 CMO ramp expected to build from Q2 and more in Q3. Management reiterated 15-20% annual growth as a minimum commitment, with EU and US certifications for Indore still pending.

segments.commentary: Launched monobactam and beta-lactamase inhibitor combination on innovator patent expiry; Sparsh completed a full quarter on the rebuilt channel with outstanding days within trade terms. Focus is on own-manufactured brands and depth within existing hospital groups.

segments.commentary: Ferticare retains leadership in recurrent implantation failure; Puregraf entered major corporate IVF chains. Zenova is shifting from injectables to prescription chronic therapies, with two first-mover launches (osteoarthritis, metabolic ovarian) due ahead.

Licensing progressed in Europe, a contract manufacturing and licensing arrangement was signed with a North American partner, and first CMO orders were received in Australia. guidance_outlook: Management commits to 15-20% year-on-year company growth as a bare minimum, with efforts aimed at growing beyond that.
Indore capacity utilisation expected to rise from about 30-35% now to around 40-45% by year-end, with the Indore liquid line targeted at about 80% utilisation within three years.
Margin expansion from Indore expected once EU certification is in place. Management says the 18% operating margin is the start of an improvement trend, not a new normal.
Management expects operating leverage to start around mid-FY28.

Indore revenue potential is INR800-1,200 crore from current capex (about INR300 crore), so combined with Navsari the maximum is about INR1,600-2,000 crore; management also cited INR1,600-1,800 crore with no further capex.
Botulinum toxin and biostimulator in-licensed products are to launch this financial year with no significant capex. Stunnox and Zarbot registrations in SE Asia and Africa take 12-18 months.

Indore is fully operational as a unit; new product lines are being added within the existing capex of about INR300 crore, with no major new infrastructure.
Indore utilisation has risen from 18-22% last year, to 20-25%, to close to 30-35% this year.
Navsari is largely capped at about INR800 crore revenue, with toxin and penem blocks not yet saturated.

Fillers market in India is estimated at about INR200 crore. Management aims to move from number 2 to number 1 in toxin plus fillers within 3-5 years.

International: aims to raise margins from 40-50% under distributor models to 15-20% higher with its own field force in Africa, Southeast Asia and South Asia. Recruitment of a regional team happened in Q1.
CHAI partnership for liposomal amphotericin B gives access to more than 100 markets; bioequivalence study due by August-September, followed by WHO PQ filing.

qa_highlights.question: How does the shift in international model (distributor-led to own-registration, field-force led) change economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is moving to own field force in Africa, Southeast Asia and South Asia once registrations and scale allow, aiming to lift margins from 40-50% under distributor models by 15-20% or more. A regional team was recruited in Q1 (one person in Mexico, one in the Philippines, two in Mumbai); the company also says it is building IP and trademarks in these markets.

qa_highlights.question: When will Indore get EU certification and does margin expansion follow, and is 18% the new normal margin?

Indore utilisation was 18-22% last year, 20-25% the year before, and close to 30-35% this year, targeted at 40-45% by year-end. Management said the 18% margin is the start of an improvement trend rather than a new normal, and that the earlier 18% period had Indore costs, depreciation and interest capitalised.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fillers (Revanesse tie-up) scale, and how big is the opportunity?

qa_highlights.question: Is 15-20% growth conservative, and can growth go beyond 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15-20% year-on-year company growth is a bare minimum, with efforts aimed at growing beyond it. Some low-yielding product mix is being squeezed out, and it was not conservative in that guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential from current capacity without further capex (analyst cited about INR2,700 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Roonghta first put FY27 expected revenue at about INR1,100 crore, with 15% annual growth taking it to about INR1,600 crore on existing facilities. Pranav Choksi said Navsari is capped at about INR800 crore, with toxin and penem not saturated, and Indore could add INR800-1,200 crore on about INR300 crore capex. The combined no-capex figure was cited as INR1,600-1,800 crore, and the total maximum as INR1,600-2,000 crore. The INR2,700 crore figure was not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned employee addition strategy, and what productivity metrics are used?
qa_highlights.answer: Most additions are at Indore, with about 50-60 people for domestic expansion, while international headcount is capped at 20-25. Employee cost growth is in line with the company's overall growth.

Gross margin fell to 46% from 51% on raw material inflation, offset by volume growth, manpower productivity, energy savings and newer businesses. H1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 10.8% versus 8.6%, and working capital days fell to 84 from 95. Management said Pyrova Energy turned operationally profitable in Q2 and targets a mid-teens EBITDA margin for the platform once rCB and pyrolysis expansion are complete.

509480|2026-06.headline: Berger Paints Q1 FY27 standalone value growth 12.7% on ~8.4% volume; operating margin 17.4%, PAT up 25.5%.

Gross margin was 39.3%, held back by delayed and partial price pass-through in industrial and protective, GI and powder coatings, where price increases landed late in the quarter. Consolidated revenue rose 12%, PBDIT rose 12.6%-15% (management cited 15% operating profit growth) with margin up about 40 bps, and PAT rose 28.6%, with the Bolex and STP subsidiaries lagging on growth. Management guided to double-digit FY27 revenue growth, a slightly better Q2 than Q1 on a year-on-year basis, and operating margin within the 15-17% range.

509480|2026-09.headline: Berger Paints Q2 FY27 standalone revenue grew 11.9% on ~8% decorative price growth, but standalone PBDIT fell 4.4% and PAT 7.3% as gross margin compressed.
509480|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue rose 11.9% in Q2 FY27 and 12.3% in H1, with volume up 3% in Q2 and 5.6% in H1, per management. Gross margin fell to 36.6% in Q2 (38.1% in H1) as double-digit raw material inflation, liquidation of high-cost inventory and delayed industrial price hikes hit margins. Q2 EBITDA margin was 10.8% (standalone), and H1 was 14.4%, below management's 15-17% guided range; a Rs 22 crore extra spend on the new Rangbanara Rahe campaign weighed on the quarter. Consolidated revenue grew 13.2% in Q2 and PBDIT 5.2%, with subsidiaries strong and the JVs (Berger Becker, BNPA) contributing; management expects Q3 and Q4 margins to recover toward the guided band.

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Double-digit value growth driven by about 8% price growth; volumes moderated as later Diwali shifted demand to Q3 and price-sensitive putty, textures and enamel de-grew. Home sealing products (roof coat, Dam Shield) and wood coatings grew strongly.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: High double-digit volume and value growth across automotive (about 5-6% of mix, growing about 31% on two-wheeler demand), protective and general industrial; gross margin fell about 5.5% as price hikes lagged raw material inflation.

segments.name: Subsidiaries and JVs
segments.commentary: Bolik's SA grew strongly; BJ and Nepal showed robust revenue and profit growth; STP revenue and operating profit grew well with margins moderating; SBL growth on pricing with profitability hit by solvent RM inflation; Berger Becker coil coatings and BNPA grew over 40% in revenue, with margins compressed (JVs contribute only 49% of profit).

guidance_outlook: Management is confident EBITDA margin will get close to the 15-17% band in Q3 and possibly Q4, supported by calibrated price increases, cost-saving initiatives and cost discipline.
Industrial price hikes: about 90% of targeted increase expected to be recovered by end-November, the balance by December.
Raw material prices (largely crude-linked) softened slightly in Q2 and that drop is expected to carry into Q3; management did not give a fixed view on month-to-month movement.
October was the highest monthly sales growth in about 25-30 months; management expects strong revenue growth in Q3 on festive demand.
Working capital to normalise as input costs stabilise; company intends to remain net cash.
Urban-market experiment (MEGA framework) to be finalised by March 2027, with acceleration from April 2027.
capex_capacity: Hindustan (Kolkata-area) plant expansion just completed, per management.
West Bengal government announced a new industrial incentive policy; company to evaluate investment scale for its Panagarh plant.
Plans for a new factory in Orissa; both new factories to be funded from internal cash rather than borrowing, with short-term borrowing possible.
Capex in new factories expected at a later date; no quantified amount given.
demand_pricing: Decorative price growth of about 8%; new entrant previously priced about 5% below industry and has now moved to industry parity but is rebating more to dealers, so competitive intensity remains.
Market share (top-6 listed companies basis) about 20.2% at H1 vs 20.3% earlier: stable, no loss or gain in the half.
Urban markets: Berger has under half its all-India share there (e.g. about 7-8% in Bangalore, lower in Pune and Mumbai), seen as a major opportunity.
Industrial price increases partly passed on; some rebates pulled back in certain decorative categories, which restrained top-line growth.
Retail store network of 2,000+ stores and tinting and point-of-sale expansion continue.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the receivables and inventory build-up in the cash flow statement, and will gross margin recovery take time?

qa_highlights.question: Will Asian Paints' backward integration into VAM/VAE and possible price cuts affect Berger's competitiveness?

qa_highlights.question: How is the marketing spend expected to behave, given past campaigns?
qa_highlights.answer: Brand building needs sustained spend; the Rangbanara Rahe corporate campaign is the first in many years. Spend will taper after launch, with bursts roughly every 7-8 months.

qa_highlights.question: Status of urban-penetration strategy, moving from walls to space, and use of free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Urban experiment is yielding positive results and will be finalised by March 2027, then accelerated from April 2027. Berger will stay in paints, coatings, construction chemicals and waterproofing; surplus cash to fund West Bengal and Orissa factories, not borrowings.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity and market share trend in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Market share about 20.2% vs 20.3% earlier, relatively stable. Management said it aims to hold share, not to gain heavily, given intense competition.

qa_highlights.question: What price increases have been pushed in industrial and the gross margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial gross margin fell about 5.5%; October price increases taken, with 90% of target expected by end-November and the rest by December. Recovery depends on crude staying at lower levels.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on crude-linked raw material prices, which are volatile; a rebound would erode the planned industrial price recovery.

rows.label: Industrial price hikes recovery

509496|2026-03.headline: Cemindia FY26 revenue crossed INR10,000 crore (INR10,061 crore, +9%) and Q4 EBITDA margin hit 15.1%, helped by one-time claims and provision releases.
509496|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating income rose to INR2,973 crore for the full year and Q4 EBITDA jumped 66% YoY to INR450 crore at a 15.1% margin. Management attributed the margin spike to one-time items: INR150 crore of claims realised (INR100 crore in Q4, partly booked as other income) and release of provisions held for metro jobs now completed. Management guided that the normal EBITDA margin is about 10-10.5%. Order book stands at INR29,000 crore, including L1 positions of about INR1,600 crore and an April win of about INR3,200 crore. FY27 guidance is revenue growth of at least 20-25%, with an order-inflow target of about INR25,000 crore.

segments.name: Group / captive EPC (Adani-linked) and data centre
segments.commentary: Data centre is a new division with 3-4 jobs secured from the group; cumulative data centre order book about INR3,000 crore. Management is keeping it within the group for now, with Vizag opportunities mentioned.

segments.name: Metro and tunnelling
segments.commentary: Bangalore and Mumbai metro jobs completed and contributed to Q4 margin. Chennai Metro has about 40% of value left, with completion expected around end-2027 to early 2028; the company owns 4 TBMs at Chennai and sold a Bangalore TBM. Tunnelling market (metro, road and other) is cited at about INR1 lakh crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue to grow at least 25% per MD's opening answer; later answers say 20-25% is quite possible on top line.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR25,000 crore, against about INR19,000 crore secured in FY26 (including L1 and April wins).
Sustainable EBITDA margin excluding other income guided at about 10-10.5%; management says it will try for more than 10%.
FY27 capex planned at INR350-400 crore, against INR260 crore in FY26.
PAT margin: management aims to maintain the same momentum and margin.
