capex_capacity: FY27 capex planned at INR350-400 crore versus INR260 crore in FY26.
Chennai Metro TBMs have completed breakthrough; about 40% of value left, completion expected around end-2027 to early 2028 (stations included in scope).
New TBMs being bought for Pune Metro and Delhi Metro; large-diameter TBM would be needed for large diameter tunnel work.
No idle TBMs at present; a TBM is typically engaged for 3-4 years on a job.
demand_pricing: Work in hand (order book) stands at INR29,000 crore versus about INR20,000-21,000 crore a year earlier; management says no legacy jobs remain.
FY26 order wins about INR14,000 crore excluding L1 and April wins; with L1 and April wins, about INR19,000 crore versus about INR7,000 crore in prior years.
Pipeline of about INR70,000 crore, of which group is about 35-40%; roads and highways and tunnelling are the main segments, each about INR1 lakh crore market.

Vadhvan port: breakwater tender and dredging and reclamation tender out; company is L1 for the breakwater job and progress has stalled since technical bid opening in October with customer reasons unknown.
Mor Sagar (JV with group, 27% stake) is at early design stage; EPC award could go to the company or another party based on price.

Around 30% of jobs have fixed-price (star price) arrangements with commodity pass-through in both directions; about 80% of jobs have a clause protecting against normal inflation but not abnormal war-driven cost spikes.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin expansion to about 12% excluding other income, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited completed metro jobs, claims realised and release of provisions kept for metro jobs; it said this is not a regular phenomenon and guided 10-10.5% going forward.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 margin came from claims?
qa_highlights.answer: INR150 crore of claims were realised for the full year, of which INR100 crore in Q4; part was booked in other income (mainly interest) and part in revenue. The claim was described as one-time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mobilisation advance and how much is interest-bearing?
qa_highlights.answer: Mobilisation advance was INR1,400 crore at March 2026, with about 90% interest-free and about 10% interest-bearing; interest terms depend on the project and the promoter-group's contract with the client.

qa_highlights.question: How is the data centre business progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: A new division has 3-4 group jobs and about INR3,000 crore of data centre orders; the focus is on group opportunities for now, with Vizag opportunities mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Adani road-tunnel project and Vadhvan?
qa_highlights.answer: The group is L1 on the road tunnel job but has not yet received the order; the company will bid if it is awarded. Vadhvan is a slow-moving project and the company is waiting on customer decisions on the breakwater and dredging tenders.

qa_highlights.question: How much inflation risk is passed through to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% of jobs are fixed-price with commodity pass-through, about 80% have normal-inflation escalation clauses, and the remainder has no protection; management expects some margin impact that will be priced into future bids.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a dividend and fundraising plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The dividend was not declared this year due to a process delay and management said it will be declared within a few weeks. No fundraising is planned as the company has adequate funds.

risks_watch: Q4 margin of 15.1% included one-time claims and provision releases; normalised margin guided at about 10-10.5%, so Q1 FY27 margin is a key test.
Vadhvan port project is slow-moving with no clarity on the timing of the customer's release of the breakwater work.
Commodity and fuel inflation (crude, cement, steel) could squeeze margins on the about 70% of jobs without full pass-through, and this is not yet quantified.
Payment risk from some state governments; management says central government payments are fine but several states have weak treasuries and some bills remain uncertified.
Dependence on group orders: group is 35-40% of the INR70,000 crore pipeline; the road-tunnel award to the group is pending.
Management could not give Bangladesh receivables or the Q1 FY27 order details beyond L1 and April wins; the call reported the Bangladesh receivables as under control.
Dividend declaration pending; the company said it will be declared within a few weeks.

509496|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 operating income rose 6% YoY to Rs 2,721 crore, EBITDA margin 10.5%, while order inflow nearly tripled to Rs 8,519 crore.
509496|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 6% YoY to Rs 2,721 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to Rs 285 crore, with margin up to 10.5% from 10.1%. PAT rose 3% to Rs 141 crore. Management said Q1 revenue was held back by Vadhvan port execution not starting, and by four newly won jobs (Munger, Pune Metro, Delhi Metro, Morsagar; about Rs 10,000-12,000 crore) that had not yet begun production. Management maintained FY27 revenue growth guidance of 25%, with the bulk of catch-up expected from Q3. A Rs 5,000 crore QIP enabling resolution was approved, but management said the timing and amount depend on future orders and market conditions.

financial_highlights.change: vs about Rs 2,900 crore in Q1 FY26 (about 3x)

financial_highlights.value: about 120 days (inventory about 30 days, WIP about 107 days)

segments.name: Marine
segments.commentary: About Rs 15,000 crore of marine jobs in the tender pipeline, including Vadhvan port (execution not started), overseas jobs in Oman and UAE, and Bangladesh work. Tuticorin Outer Harbour and Vizag port also mentioned.

segments.name: Data centre
segments.commentary: Five Navi Mumbai projects (three of 140 MW, one of 130 MW and two of 30 MW) are under way; a Vizag civil job has also been secured. Total work is about 320-400 MW, with electromechanical work possibly later.

segments.name: Bangladesh transmission project
segments.commentary: Execution is under control. Completion is now guided for September/October 2026 (earlier June 2026 timing was cited by an analyst). Receivables are about Rs 178 crore plus retention.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 25% (management also said 20-25% growth is achievable for a few years).
FY27 order inflow target of about Rs 25,000 crore; Rs 8,519 crore secured in Q1 and about Rs 1,247 crore added in July, with L1 positions of about Rs 900-1,000 crore.
Q3 and Q4 expected to be much better than Q1; Q2 seen as weak because of monsoon. Management cited last year's Q1 of Rs 2,500 crore, Q2 Rs 2,100 crore and Q4 Rs 3,000 crore as the pattern.
FY27 capex guided at Rs 350-400 crore, barring exceptional plant purchases such as TBMs for large road tunnels.
Working capital expected to stay at 110-120 days; gross debt expected to rise about 10-20% and at least 20-25% if top line grows 25%.

Rs 5,000 crore QIP is an enabling resolution. Management said part is for capex (Rs 4,000-5,000 crore range cited for capex needs) and part for working capital and possibly inorganic growth, with timing dependent on orders and markets.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex additions were Rs 81 crore; FY27 capex guided at Rs 350-400 crore.
Large diameter road tunnel jobs would need tunnel boring machines, raising capex well above the normal run-rate.
Management said plant older than five years is not permitted on many projects, which raises replacement capex needs.
Data centre capacity is about 320-400 MW in progress; Navi Mumbai civil works already in place.
Management said current operating capacity allows about Rs 5,000 crore of quarterly revenue, which the analyst asked about and management confirmed.
demand_pricing: Work-in-hand is about Rs 31,000 crore versus Rs 18,000-20,000 crore earlier; about Rs 12,000 crore of it had no progress yet (Munger, DMRC, Pune Metro, Morsagar).

Adani group makes up about 50% of the order book (Rs 6,000 crore of Q1 orders from the group and Rs 2,500 crore from outside). Group work is competitively bid with no fixed price, and some material is supplied free by the client.

Bid pipeline is about Rs 90,000 crore, with a hit ratio of about 15% (earlier about 20%). Six segments each carry about Rs 15,000-20,000 crore: marine, underground metro, airports, data centre, highways and bridges, and water.
Export share of order book is about 2-3%.
Management expects margin to hold in double digits, with contingency built into estimates for geopolitical and commodity risk. A government agency cut performance guarantees from 10% to 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise Rs 5,000 crore via QIP when the company is net-cash and the order book is already Rs 31,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the money is for growth, with part for plant and equipment, part for inorganic growth, and part for working capital. It also said timing depends on market conditions and near-term visibility, and that little of it would be used this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected revenue trajectory and why is growth lagging order book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Vadhvan (zero production so far), about Rs 10,000-12,000 crore of newly won jobs that need 6-7 months of design and mobilisation, and Abu Dhabi work that has only just picked up. It guided for 25% FY27 growth, with Q3 and Q4 stronger.

qa_highlights.question: What is Vadhvan port execution status?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution has not started. Management said pending issues are outside its control, with no timeline set; it hopes work will resume soon.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Bangladesh project timeline moved and what is its status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution remains on plan for September/October 2026. Monsoon-driven river conditions and deep-water foundation work are the constraints, and a different technology is being used. Receivables are about Rs 178 crore plus retention.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-25% growth sustainable, and what capex does it need?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 20-25% growth is possible over coming years. Normal segments (marine, road, industrial, airport) need about Rs 300-400 crore capex a year, but a Rs 10,000 crore road tunnel would need much more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the marine and overall competitive landscape?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are about three major marine players, with about five including others. Competition is intense and price-driven, and the hit ratio is about 15%.

risks_watch: Vadhvan port execution has not started and management says the pending issues are outside its control with no timeline; a large share of expected revenue depends on it.

About Rs 10,000-12,000 crore of newly won jobs (Munger, Pune Metro, Delhi Metro, Morsagar) need 6-7 months of design and mobilisation; their revenue contribution from Q3 is the main test of the 25% FY27 guidance.

Q2 is expected to be weak due to monsoon, and Bangladesh transmission completion has slipped to September/October 2026 from an earlier June 2026 timing, with river and deep-water foundation constraints.
Rs 5,000 crore QIP is only an enabling resolution with timing tied to orders and markets; watch how much is actually raised and deployed into plant, inorganic growth and working capital.
Hit ratio has fallen to about 15% from about 20% as bidding volume rises; about 50% of the order book and pipeline is from the Adani group, and labour shortages were acknowledged.

Yes, you are right. Absolutely right.
Jayanta Basu: Yes. 25%.

509496|2026-09.headline: Cemindia Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR2,749 crore, with order book at a record INR32,715 crore and EBITDA margin at 10.2%.
509496|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 total operating income was INR2,749 crore (+25% YoY) and EBITDA INR280 crore (+15% YoY), with EBITDA margin easing to 10.2% from 11.1%. PAT rose 21% YoY to INR131 crore. H1 operating income was INR5,470 crore (+15%) and PAT INR271 crore (+10.8%). Management said Q2 revenue was roughly flat on Q1, unusual for a seasonally weaker quarter, and that a INR1,400 crore QIP and three rating upgrades (ICRA AA, CARE AA-, CRISIL AA, all Stable) were completed. Order book reached INR32,715 crore after INR5,968 crore of wins since quarter start.

segments.name: Marine / ports
segments.commentary: Dhamra Port (INR800 crore) and Project Varsha for Indian Navy outer harbour (INR700 crore) won in Q2. Jatadhari Port marine job nearing completion. Vadhavan Port work restarted; port order book about INR1,500 crore.

segments.name: Metro / urban infra

qa_highlights.question: Q2 order inflow details and October wins?

qa_highlights.question: Is revenue guidance of 20-25% still valid, and what is capex outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Data centre execution timelines and margins?

qa_highlights.question: Is Adani/group tunnel project and China TBM restriction an issue?

qa_highlights.question: ROE pressure from capex and dilution?

qa_highlights.answer: Total about INR5,500 crores including 20,000 t existing (about INR2,350 crores), 24,000 t additional (about INR1,600 crores), graphene INR500 crores, crucible INR475 crores, RePlus expansion INR250 crores spent and INR230 crores for a Gujarat BESS IPP project.

qa_highlights.question: How is capex phased by year and what is the EBITDA margin outlook for each business?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR2,300 crores in FY27, INR1,600-1,700 crores in FY28, balance in FY29. Anode EBITDA 28-33% rising above 35% with crucible integration; graphene above 45%; RePlus around 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Are there confirmed orders for the planned capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said contracts are on a no-name basis, with 3-4 LOIs signed and 3-4 more expected in months; customer demand led the move from 20,000 t to 44,000 t; Dewas site capped at 44,000 t.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ramp-up plan for anode capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: First-year utilisation assumed at 35% because it is a large construction plant; management said ramp from 50% to 90% is not a problem given linear equipment; first 20,000 t mostly exports.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the power segment EBIT margin so high in Q2 and how much is one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher one-time receipts in Q2 (transmission-line ISTS arrears, insurance gain); about 40% of the INR190 crores Power EBIT is one-time and about 60% recurring, so the 40% will not recur in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the solar project and the hydro plans?
qa_highlights.answer: A 300 MW standalone C&I solar project at about INR1,200 crores, around 12 months from completion, not yet signed so excluded from capex; management cited double-digit IRR. Management said it is not pursuing many more C&I projects.

qa_highlights.question: Can cash be upstreamed between subsidiaries given the Statkraft-linked debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating options to consolidate the power business and deploy cash, but asked for a few quarters before updating.

capex_capacity: Total capex across anode (20,000 t Dewas Phase 1 plus 24,000 t Phase 2), RePlus expansion, crucible and graphene is about INR5,500 crores; current 20,000 t anode capex about INR2,350 crores, additional 24,000 t about INR1,600 crores, graphene INR500 crores, crucible (80,000 units) INR475 crores, RePlus 1 GWh to 6 GWh INR250 crores spent so far, plus INR230 crores on a BESS IPP project in Gujarat.
Phased capex: about INR2,300 crores in FY27, INR1,600-1,700 crores in FY28, balance in FY29. Capex of about INR490 crores in H1 FY27, largely anode.

Dewas Phase 1 (20,000 t) 61% complete, commercial commissioning targeted June 2027; Phase 2 takes capacity to 44,000 t by March 2029 on the same 105-acre site; management said 60,000 t was the site's preferred limit but 44,000 t is the maximum fit.

Graphene: 10 t pilot running; 500 t commercial plant targeted by September 2028 in a new location, split into 200 t (already started) and 300 t delayed pending land and environmental permissions; graphene asset turn about 1:1, anode about 0.8x.

Proposed 300 MW standalone C&I solar project at about INR1,200 crores, expected in about 12 months, excluded from capex as it is not yet signed; RePlus 5 GWh capacity COD cited as March 2027 by the RePlus CEO.
demand_pricing: Management cited global Li-ion battery production rising from about 3 TWh in 2026 to 8 TWh by 2035, and graphite anode demand from about 2.9 million t to 8 million t over the same period; non-China anode demand projected above 1 million t by 2030.

Anode: over 100,000 t of customer MOUs in advanced discussions; 3-4 LOIs signed and 3-4 more expected in the next few months; contracts on a no-name basis. Customers include non-Chinese cell makers in Korea, Japan, US, Germany and Middle East.

Anode raw material: green petroleum coke and power make up more than 60% of cost; main suppliers from US, UK and Japan. Average anode cost about INR9 lakh/t blended (INR11 lakh/t on first 20,000 t, INR6 lakh/t on next 24,000 t). First 20,000 t mostly for export.
Graphene: about 90 t of orders and LOIs; management guides EBITDA margin of 40-45% and said no pricing disclosed; first 90 t supply to start in H2 FY28.

Power: normative about 1,000 MU/yr, 75:25 H1:H2 split; PLF 43-44%; merchant realisation about INR6-6.5/unit this year; peaking power about 30% of output at around INR9-10/unit; management guides power EBITDA of INR350 crores on lower prices.
RePlus: EBITDA around 10% (plus or minus 1-2%); 70-80% of business is EPC and 20-30% manufacturing and supply, moving to 50:50 next year and about 20% EPC in two years.
Crucible: about 40% cheaper than imports per management; external crucible realisation and margins guided at around 30-40%; in-house need peaks at 40,000-45,000 t.

Competition: China is sole crucible producer today; management said the company was ahead of other Indian anode entrants given 12-18 month qualification cycles. Graphite electrode revenue fell about 20-23% QoQ per an analyst, deferred to a separate call.

509675|2026-03.headline: BirlaNu Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 9% YoY to Rs 1,010 crore; standalone EBITDA margin up ~380 bps, but Parador impairment of Rs 74 crore hit standalone books.
509675|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a transition year, with subdued demand, pricing pressure and Middle East-driven volatility. Q4 improved: consolidated revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs 1,010 crore and standalone EBITDA margin expanded about 380 bps, helped by a Rs 5 crore Clean Coats dividend and resin price spikes in March. Full-year consolidated revenue was Rs 3,730 crore (+3%), while standalone EBITDA rose 39% to Rs 146 crore, aided by Rs 22 crore Clean Coats dividend and Rs 7 crore asset-sale profit. A Rs 74 crore diminution provision on the BirlaNu International GmbH (Parador) investment was booked as an exceptional item in standalone accounts, and Parador posted a Rs 35 crore operating loss in Q4 including a Rs 19 crore severance provision. Total debt was Rs 851 crore at year-end, down from Rs 929 crore in December.

segments.name: Roofs
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 275 crore (+8% YoY, +18% QoQ); FY26 revenue broadly stable at Rs 1,139 crore. Management says it holds market leadership and pricing premium, with margins largely stable.

segments.name: Walls
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 161 crore (+14% YoY); FY26 revenue Rs 610 crore (+13%). Mix about 60% AAC Blocks, 25% Panels, 15% Boards; Panels and Boards grew 20-25% in FY26; Q4 blended volume growth above 20%. Blocks, Panels and Boards are all at full capacity utilisation.

segments.name: Construction Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 37 crore (+58% YoY); FY26 revenue Rs 117 crore (+45%), crossing Rs 100 crore milestone. Ex-Clean Coats growth was 25% for FY26; Clean Coats contributed Rs 20 crore over 4.5 months since acquisition.

segments.name: Pipes
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 147 crore (+4% YoY, ~+30% QoQ per CEO); FY26 revenue Rs 495 crore (-8%) with flat volumes. Q4 EBITDA margin up ~1,300 bps YoY on March resin price spike and inventory revaluation; FY26 margin up 280 bps. CPVC ~39-40% of mix, uPVC/SWR/pressure pipes the rest; Q4 volume growth about 2-3%.

segments.name: Parador (Europe)
segments.commentary: Revenue down 9% YoY in euro terms in Q4 and 7% for FY26; operating loss Rs 35 crore in Q4 including Rs 19 crore severance. Management expects gradual recovery through FY27 from retail reboot and premium Engineered Wood range.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Pipes to see a stronger recovery in FY27, supported by government spending and infrastructure demand; resin prices expected to stabilise over coming months.
Parador: expects sales bounce-back in FY27 with positive profitability flow-through; no quantified target given.
Brownfield Walls capacity expansions expected to come on-stream within FY27 (around Q3 at latest); Nellore greenfield boards plant (HD and designer boards) on track.
BCG value enhancement savings expected to be fully realised from FY27 onwards.
Management aspires to double-digit EBITDA margins via portfolio mix shift toward Construction Chemicals and Walls; no timeline given beyond 2-3 years.
Roofs: price differential versus steel roofing is high, giving pricing headroom and substitution opportunity; some input-cost inflation expected to be partly offset by price increases.
capex_capacity: Nellore, Andhra Pradesh greenfield boards plant is on track against defined execution milestones; will add value-added HD and designer boards.
OPVC facility in Patna is fully commissioned.
Brownfield Walls expansions expected to come on-stream in FY27, hopefully by start or around Q3.
Pipes: capacity to scale a further 30-40% over current output without fresh investment; footprint across North, South, East and West India; over 3,000 SKUs.
Walls: Chennai new line utilisation improved during FY26.
demand_pricing: Roofs: management cites good demand momentum over the last 2-3 months, better than the last couple of years, with rural resilience and substitution away from steel roofing as steel prices rallied.
Pipes: PVC resin prices hit multiyear lows, then rose about 60% in March over 3-4 weeks and a further 25-30% in April; government spending on water/JJM showed early green shoots from Q4.
Parador: weak European demand, intensified competition and softer pricing; Engineered Wood mid-end hit by cheaper Chinese imports, so premium range launched in February.
Middle East conflict drove energy and logistics volatility, rupee depreciation and imported raw material inflation; some orders deferred from March into FY27.
Pricing pressure persisted in Walls through FY26, offset by cost discipline.

qa_highlights.question: Given the Parador impairment, when will the company take a final call on the European subsidiary after about 8 years of losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is applying external advisers' recommended actions at Parador, some visible and some not, and acts on data and order books rather than hope; no specific exit decision was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of Construction Chemicals growth including and excluding Clean Coats?
qa_highlights.answer: Including Clean Coats, FY26 growth was 45% and Q4 growth 58%; excluding Clean Coats, FY26 growth was 25%. Clean Coats contributed Rs 20 crore over 4.5 months.

qa_highlights.question: Pipes product mix and the anti-dumping duty removal?
qa_highlights.answer: CPVC is about 39-40% of pipes mix and uPVC and other products the rest. Management said the duty removal was a government step taken in early April to curb volatility; it declined to comment on industry lobbying.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Parador's Q4 margin so negative beyond severance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no other operational issues; the loss was mainly lower revenue and volumes as orders deferred after the early-March war disruption.

qa_highlights.question: How is Parador positioned in India and against lower-priced competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Positioned at the premium end as a Made in Germany product, targeting metros and large cities with a dedicated sales team; landed cost and price sensitivity were flagged as challenges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt capacity and the impact of the employee cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said consolidated equity is about Rs 1,100 crore against debt of about Rs 850 crore, with room for another Rs 200-250 crore. Management said the employee cost comparison needs reconciliation and that headcount is reviewed constantly.

qa_highlights.question: Walls volume growth, capacity utilisation and segment mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 Walls blended volume growth above 20%; Blocks, Panels and Boards all at full utilisation; mix about 60% Blocks, 25% Panels, 15% Boards.

risks_watch: Parador: further impairments or severance in FY27, and whether European sales recover as management expects.
Pipes: PVC resin price volatility, reversal of the March spike, and the anti-dumping duty removal ending June; channel stocking or destocking risk.
Standalone margin sustainability: Q4 benefited from one-offs (Clean Coats dividend Rs 5 crore, inventory revaluation, asset-sale gains).

Balance sheet: debt at Rs 851 crore; management indicated capacity for Rs 200-250 crore more; inorganic growth and $1 billion revenue ambition may require equity or cash accrual support, and the promoter stance was not addressed.
Input cost inflation from rupee depreciation, freight, cement, fibre and energy; pricing pass-through in Roofs is not yet confirmed.

509675|2026-06.headline: BirlaNu Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.6% to Rs 1,174 crores and EBITDA 35% to Rs 80 crores, with Parador still loss-making at Rs 13 crores.
509675|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue grew 10% to Rs 824 crores and EBITDA rose nearly 70% to Rs 97 crores, with margins up over 420 bps, led by Roofs and Pipes. Pipes revenue fell 11% and volumes fell 27% on a sharp PVC resin price swing, yet EBITDA margin expanded 660 bps on mix and pricing. Parador swung to a Rs 13 crore EBITDA loss, which management attributed mostly to timing items expected to normalise in H2. Gross borrowings fell about Rs 100 crores to Rs 758 crores and working capital was cut by about Rs 100 crores year-on-year.

qa_highlights.answer: Breaches were on debt-equity covenants; borrowings were Rs 852 crores at March 2026 and Rs 758 crores at June 2026, and they will stay elevated near term until Nellore starts contributing from late FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How does Parador grow over the next 2-3 years and what is the cost upside?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees at least Rs 20-30 million of added revenue from US, India, UK and Middle East commercial channels, DIY expansion in Europe, and Italy and Eastern Europe orders; BCG cost programme targets at least 300-400 bps EBITDA uplift.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Boards market and why is BirlaNu's margin below the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Market is Rs 1,500-2,000 crores growing 10-14%; the company's wall segment blended margin is 10-11% while new standalone board plants target 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Roofs margins and growth one-offs or sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-offs or inventory gains; growth was about 10% volume plus price, and the mix is primarily secondary sales in the season.

qa_highlights.question: Is Parador manufacturing moving to India, and is a rights issue planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Options including India are being evaluated for cost-to-serve and supply-chain diversification, subject to quality; the CFO said debt-equity is 0.68x and the Board decides on any rights issue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Telangana plant's economics and the Nellore capex status?
qa_highlights.answer: Telangana asset turn is 0.9x on about Rs 145-150 crores investment excluding land; Nellore is in civil construction with about 90-100% of orders placed.

509675|2026-09.headline: BirlaNu India business revenue rose 17.3% to Rs 588 crore with EBITDA of Rs 40 crore (6.8% margin), while Parador's Rs 90 crore extra provision weighed on consolidated results.

Management stated confidence in H2 and a strong FY27, while Parador remained the main focus of analyst pushback. Total debt rose to Rs 896 crore from Rs 852 crore at March 31, driven by greenfield capex.

509820|2026-03.headline: Huhtamaki India Q1 FY26 EBITDA up 24.8% YoY on mix and efficiency; sales up only ~10 bps, EBIT hit by INR 88 mn prior-period depreciation charge.
509820|2026-03.overview: Management reported sales broadly flat (up about 10 bps YoY) with EBITDA up 24.8% YoY, attributed to higher-value sales mix and operational efficiency. Reported EBIT was about INR 386 mn after a one-off INR 88 mn depreciation charge for prior two years (WDV instead of SLM error), with EBIT margin ex-charge at about 8% (27.8% EBIT margin ex-charge is stated in the call and appears to be an inconsistent figure relative to the 8% quoted). Reported PAT of about INR 256 crore was roughly 2% lower YoY; management said it rose about 23.1% excluding the prior-year charge. Raw material costs rose sharply from end-March on the Middle East conflict; management said most of the increase was passed through to customers, with low-to-medium double-digit RM impact.

Customers came with panic-driven volume requests during the conflict; management said demand has since stabilised with no significant change.
Competition: large multinational customers grow slowly; smaller regional Indian players grow faster. Management said it is not chasing low-value volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material cost impact post-war and is availability an issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices rose from end-March and are volatile; low-to-medium double-digit RM impact overall. Availability is not an issue given global procurement, though shipments from overseas can be delayed. Most costs passed to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments are seeing demand post-war and how is cost affecting demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers initially over-ordered in panic, then volumes stabilised. No significant demand change; large FMCG customers grow 2-5%, regional customers faster.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company losing share given the 10-12% market growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the market includes multinationals and smaller regional Indian players growing faster; the company is selective and focused on innovation and premium customers, so growth is in line with its value proposition. Amit Gupta said the market definition includes paper and is not comparable.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the jump in other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest on an income tax refund (about INR 6.5 crore), higher FD interest, and FX gains on exports from rupee weakness. Management said several one-offs offset this.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in other expenses from INR 95 crore to INR 106 crore QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase is not substantial, expense ratios are declining as a percentage of sales, and the one-offs include provision reversals and the INR 88 mn depreciation charge plus a property charge.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 100 crore ECB repayment to the parent extended from Feb 2026 to June 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: The ECB loan from the parent follows RBI tenure guidelines; part has been repaid and the balance is payable by June 2027. Servicing cost is linked to FD returns, so no negative impact, per management.

EBITDA margin expanded to 10.5% from 8.3%, and PBT rose 77% to INR559 crore, with EPS up about 77%. H1 sales grew close to 12% and H1 EBIT margin was hit by a one-time INR8.8 crore prior-period depreciation charge; excluding it, EBIT margin was 7.6%. 509820|2026-09.headline: Huhtamaki India Q3 net sales rose about 24% to INR748 crore with volume up about 7%, while reported PAT fell 19% to INR30 crore on a one-time Baddi charge.

511034|2026-06.headline: Jindal Drilling Q1 FY27: ONGC awarded a rig contract at ~INR45 lakh/day fixed; order book INR1,310 crore, with three rigs to dehire later in FY27.
511034|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as fairly good and broadly in line with expectations, with total revenue flat over the previous couple of quarters. EBITDA was stable; the variation in other expenses was driven by forex, which was more pronounced in Q4 FY26 and less so in Q1 FY27. The key development was a new ONGC contract for Jindal Pioneer, which is under refurbishment in UAE with deployment targeted for October 2026. The order book stands at INR1,310 crore, and three rigs are expected to dehire within FY27, which management said will reduce H2 revenue. The call also disclosed a JV loss tied to Pioneer refurbishment and an update on a long-running ONGC legal dispute.

Discovery-I and Jindal Star contracts had a slight extension in duration (per presentation).

Three rigs dehiring in later FY27 will need 4-6 months refurbishment each, at an estimated INR90-110 crore per rig.
Company acquired one rig in FY25 and refurbished it; cash conserved for upcoming refurbishments.
Tenders must be submitted separately for each rig owned, though multi-rig tenders are possible.
demand_pricing: Pioneer contract awarded at fixed INR45 lakh/day (approx.), INR-denominated; management said the rate was pushed down from its USD62,000/day bid to about USD47,800/day.

Redeployment of dehired rigs has been difficult for all drillers over the past two years; management expects the three dehiring rigs to be re-hired, citing the Government of India's Samudra Manthan exercise.
Day rates for the next three rigs expected to improve, though management declined to guide on rates; order book shows wide day-rate variation.
Focus is domestic (ONGC); international deployment considered only if opportunities arise, given existing-participant preference and counterparty and country risk.
Management could not say how many competing rigs are available in the market.

qa_highlights.question: Likelihood, timing and rates for renewal of the three rigs expiring in 2026?

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 FY27 revenue fall materially with three of six rigs out of contract?

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR denomination of the new contract fixed, and will INR or USD apply going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed day rate of about INR45 lakh, INR-denominated. Management will update on whether future tenders are in USD or INR next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a loss in the JV, and will it return to profit?
qa_highlights.answer: The JV was the seller of Pioneer and is funding refurbishment to bring the rig to contracted condition, which is causing the loss in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Any acquisitions planned given improved cash and lower debt?
qa_highlights.answer: No acquisitions planned. Focus is on redeploying three dehiring rigs, and cash is needed for refurbishments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ONGC dispute status and potential exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: No material update; the case has run 14-15 years and is in Supreme Court on appeal by ONGC. Company has received funds; if it loses (considered remote), it would repay about INR163 crore (INR63 crore USD receivable plus interest and forex).

511144|2026-06.headline: Axis Solutions Q1 FY27 revenue rose 78% YoY to ₹48.98 crore, with EBITDA up 122% to ₹6.21 crore and PAT up 77% to ₹3.09 crore.

PAT rose 77% to ₹3.09 crore, but PAT margin was flat at about 6.3% as tax was provided for the first time this year. Management gave no numeric FY27 guidance, only qualitative comments that growth and profit would be "very, very good". Emerging segments (hydrogen storage, Kavach, EV charging) are still pre-revenue, and the company said hydrogen margins are not yet in the financials.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Axis is in proof-of-concept with several companies and got approval for Kavach. No Kavach orders were disclosed.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said hydrogen revenue and margins are not yet in the financials. It said one industrial engineering and systems patent is in progress.

qa_highlights.answer: MRO, AMC and warranty revenue is about 5-6% of total revenue and is expected to rise over one to two years.

qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give utilisation or peak revenue. It said products are customised rather than batch-produced, and the facilities would not constrain the top line.

511147|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 26% to about INR111 crore and PAT rose 77% to INR6.14 crore, while Q4 growth slowed on macro and war-related travel weakness.
511147|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a record year, with revenue crossing about INR111 crore for the first time, PBT of INR8.03 crore and PAT of INR6.14 crore, and the company stated it remains debt-free. Q4 was hit by macro volatility, especially in March, from the US-Israel-Iran conflict and lower US student travel, though management said Q4 revenue still grew 22% and GTO grew 16%. Management highlighted the FEMA 401/2026 RBI circular, which expands AD-II scope to trade remittances and family maintenance and allows Forex Correspondent (FXC) appointments, and said it has recommended a 15% dividend. Management also acknowledged that rupee credit cards with zero cross-currency markup have taken share from forex cards in leisure travel, and that leisure market volumes contracted about 25% from March.

segments.name: Student
segments.commentary: Largest growth driver per management; overall market contracted about 20% in the year while the company gained share. Loan-funded students growing while own-funds students contracted after TCS was cut to 2%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Over 900 corporates served; management cited a 95.62% CAGR. Named clients include Accenture, Siemens, EY, Zoho, Tech Mahindra and, recently, Adani.

segments.name: Retail / leisure
segments.commentary: Card business declined in FY26 on lower US student traffic and competition from rupee credit cards; leisure market down about 25% since March. Management described this as a calibrated, value-led push with a minimum margin per transaction.

segments.name: Prepaid cards
segments.commentary: Four products (three plastics and one digital-only, Uni-Z launched last month). Switch Card supports 30 currencies; Xplorer Metal card is by invitation. Samsung Pay and Google Pay tokenisation planned this year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 to be a challenging, linear quarter with leisure travel down roughly 25% from March, and expects the next one to two months to remain tough.
Trade remittances expected to become a material business in 12 to 18 months; family maintenance (about $3 billion market) to be a growth area.
FXC network expected to expand through the model over the next 12 to 15 months, with Spice Money group network and NBFC/retail partners as possible distribution.
Trade remittance margins expected 20-30 bps, below current blended levels, as competition rises.
Target to raise digital/automated share of transactions from about 60% to 80% this year.
Management did not give numerical FY27 targets for cards or revenue; it said Q2 to Q4 are peak months and FY27 mix will change materially.
capex_capacity: Network kept lean at 21+ branches (down from 35 when the CEO took over, 16 in COVID); expansion planned mainly through FXC appointments rather than owned branches.
Company is evaluating whether to apply for a PA-CB licence.
Working on multiple payment rails for faster, holiday-enabled remittances and a student fee-remittance platform.
Smart Agent Platform, FPaaS, Smart Corporate Platform and consumer app run on a unified payments stack.
demand_pricing: Q4 traffic hit in March by the US-Israel-Iran conflict; leisure market contracted about 25% from March to May 2026 per management.
Rupee credit cards with zero cross-currency markup and lounge perks have taken a large share of international spend (management estimate about 60%), with credit card spend outside LRS and TCS.
Management says it will not price at a loss; pricing uses interbank rates with a small card fulfilment fee on the Switch card.
B2B and corporate make up about 80-85% of business; partner commissions and referral fees are a larger share of costs.
Retail customer lifetime value is quoted at about INR1,000 of annual income per traveller versus high digital CAC.
Management expects more competition after the RBI circular, with margin pressure; trade remittances may run at 20-30 bps margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new RBI circular affect volumes, revenue and margins over the next one to two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said scope has expanded to trade and non-trade current account transactions, with no negative impact from the circular itself, but competition will pressure margins. Trade remittance margins are expected at 20-30 bps; current net margin is 0.6-0.8%.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will be most affected by the new regulations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split out the impact by segment. It said the new trade and family maintenance categories open new growth areas, and that retail/leisure faces the most pressure from credit cards.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company compete with low-priced small players on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay competitive but will not work at a loss per transaction, citing a minimum margin policy and a digital platform for each segment. It acknowledged its retail pricing may not be the lowest.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise FY26 revenue, volume, customer and new-product breakdown; agent commissions versus branch revenue; CAC; card KPIs and FY27 targets
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave only broad-based answers: B2B and corporate are 80-85% of business, partner commissions are higher as a B2B company, and digital CAC is high. It declined to give specific numbers and said detailed data would be shared through the company's written channel.

qa_highlights.question: How does Scapia (bank-sponsored card) compare, and how are rupee credit cards affecting forex cards?

511147|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 turnover rose 41.2% YoY to INR2,914 crores, revenue up 30% to INR44.58 crores, PBT up 9.6% to INR5.33 crores.

511196|2026-03.headline: Can Fin Homes FY26 disbursements hit INR10,531 crore, just above guidance, with Q4 a record INR3,245 crore; FY27 disbursement target INR13,000 crore.
511196|2026-03.overview: FY26 disbursements of INR10,531 crore marginally beat the INR10,500 crore guidance, with each quarter setting a new peak and Q4 at INR3,245 crore. AUM growth was about 10.44% as rundown ran about INR600 crore above the INR6,000 crore assumption. Karnataka grew 7% in disbursements after e-khata issues, and Telangana ended roughly flat at INR1,147 crore versus INR1,198 crore. Q4 included two one-offs: INR46 crore additional DTA provision on standard assets and INR13.5 crore tax refund gain; management says underlying FY26 profit was INR1,027 crore, up 20% from INR857 crore. Around 85% of the book has moved to quarterly reset, with the 50 bps pass-through and a 15 bps cut in January leaving an opening yield near 9.8% and spread of about 2.8%.

Special-rate threshold moved from INR 20 lakh to INR 25 lakh, customer re-rating parameters and EWS/OTMS monitoring added, and 82% of loans now have CIBIL above 700 (vs about 75% earlier). Expect some indirect rise in rejection ratios; 80% of business comes via DSA.

qa_highlights.question: Status of IT rollout (LOS, LMS, report generation) and any impact on disbursement targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Pilot in 5 branches went live on 8 July 2026 using 30 June data, processing sanctions, disbursements, NACH, BBPS and closures with only minor teething issues. Remaining 245 branches to move in month-end tranches (July, August, September), with a further update around September; INR 3,000 crore Q2 target unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and blended yield by segment; are there trade-offs by ticket size?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended yield 9.81% (9.82% last year). Best rate about 8.4% for salaried, CIBIL above 725, loans of INR 25 lakh plus; highest about 12.5% for non-salaried, non-housing, S3 customers.

qa_highlights.question: Housing vs non-housing and salaried vs self-employed growth; number of loans; run-rate going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Housing disbursements INR 1,650 crore (+28% YoY) and LAP INR 958 crore (+32%); salaried +21%, SENP +44%. Management gave amounts only, not loan account counts. FY27 disbursement target INR 13,000 crore unchanged, with a possible push to INR 13,200-13,400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the IT-sector hiring slowdown in Bangalore affecting home loan offtake or policy?
qa_highlights.answer: No major impact seen so far: Karnataka grew 18% YoY and Telangana slightly more (partly base effect). IT-sector customers are about 6% of the base, with top IT employers barely represented. Karnataka NPA was lower in absolute terms at March 2026 vs March 2025, with only a marginal June increase.

qa_highlights.question: Any opex surprises in FY27 and how far is APF exposure per project capped?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 40 crore of further IT-related cost to come, with AMCs and depreciation starting; salary, rent and other costs in line with last year. Cost-to-income about 19.5% for FY27, trending toward 18% in about three years. APF exposure capped at 10% of the book per project.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the book rundown elevated for four quarters, and is the 4% level the new normal? Also, how does the best-rate gap to banks affect pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crore (vs INR 976 crore) drove the rundown, as borrowers under change-in-tenure kept EMIs constant and paid down principal. BT-outs were INR 408 crore (vs INR 400 crore), and other closures INR 377 crore (vs INR 360 crore). Best rate gap widened from 55 bps to over 100 bps; management is exploring deposit conversion and bureau alerts for retention.

qa_highlights.question: Can ROA of about 2.4% and ROE of about 18% be achieved in FY27 given higher opex and the soft Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 ROA was 2.39% (2.53% last year) and ROE 18%+. Management said the cost impact is already visible and expects to manage ROA, with NIM and spread on track and credit cost not a concern. Q1 NPA rise was only INR 17-18 crore vs INR 45 crore last Q1 FY26.

risks_watch: Book rundown: part-prepayments of INR 1,857 crore in Q1 (INR 1,072 crore part-prepay) mean FY27 disbursements may need to exceed INR 13,000 crore to hold 14% AUM growth; Q2 target is INR 3,000 crore.

IT rollout: 245 remaining branches migrate in month-end tranches through September; update expected around September. Management noted 50-100 branches will need more handholding than the 5-branch pilot.
Cost of funds: new bank loans priced at 7.25-7.5% vs 6.95% last year; NIM guidance of 3.81%+ depends on incremental-only pass-through and yield mix shift.
Competitive pricing gap: best rate spread to banks/larger players widened to over 100 bps from 55 bps; LIC and Bajaj Housing (growing about 25-30% per analyst) are main rivals.
Asset quality: SENP current NPA about 1.45-1.5% vs about 0.6-0.63% for salaried; IT-sector and Karnataka exposure monitored with early-warning signals; credit cost guided at 10 bps.
Opex: cost-to-income moved from about 18% to 19%+ in Q1, FY27 guided near 19.5%; about INR 40 crore of further IT costs yet to come.
key_quotes: So against INR 2,500 crores, which was what was planned and what was projected, we have achieved INR2,609 crores.
So, we are confident that the NIM will be maintained at 3.81% plus and we should not have a problem in that.
And so the 10 bps that we have been talking about, definitely doesn't look to be a challenge this year.

The major challenge or the major portion from where our run down is happening is actually amortization and more importantly, part prepayment where customers are making more payments every month, and but the loans are still with us.

511196|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 disbursements fell to INR2,375 crore as Project Tejas IT migration hit branches; FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore held.
511196|2026-09.overview: Can Fin Homes completed the full go-live of Project Tejas (IT transformation) across all branches, with the final ~93 old branches and new branches moving live from 1 October 2026. Disbursements for the quarter were INR2,375 crore, net of about INR29 crore of NHB-mandated cancellation netting, and management attributed the shortfall to one-time migration and process changes plus a Telangana Section 22 verification issue. Management held FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore and AUM growth of 13-14%, and guided FY28 disbursement of INR16,000 crore with 15%+ AUM growth. Prepayments eased to INR1,795 crore from INR1,857 crore in Q1, and the company passed on a 10 bps housing rate hike effective 8 October 2026.

segments.name: Branches live on new system (Project Tejas)
segments.commentary: Rollout in phases: 11 branches in July (5 old, 6 new), 89 in August (75 old, 14 new), 77 old in September and 98 in October (93 old plus 5 new). Disbursements at branches during their go-live month dropped about 70-75%, recovering to 80-90% of prior run-rate the following month.

segments.name: Branches not yet migrated (93-branch cohort)
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursement was INR435 crore in Q1 and rose to INR454, INR458, INR424 and INR481 crore in the months of July-September per management's slide 20 data (management's figures; not independently verified).

segments.name: Sales team channel
segments.commentary: Sales team headcount about 90 now, targeted at 150 by year-end and 250 in FY28; management expects INR1,500-1,600 crore from sales in FY27 versus INR560 crore in H1.

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: Disbursement has stabilised at INR230-250 crore per period, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement guidance held at INR13,000 crore (20%+ growth over INR10,500 crore in FY26); Q3 target about INR3,500 crore with the shortfall to be recovered in Q4.
FY27 AUM growth guidance of 13-14%, closer to 14%; management said the 15% AUM growth figure for FY28 is a resultant of disbursement and rundown.
FY28 disbursement internal target INR16,000 crore (about 22% growth), implying 15%+ AUM growth, closer to 15.5%.

Spread and NIM guidance of 2.75% and 3.75% maintained; management said it will pass through rate hikes, with about 12-13 bps of liability cost increase on the full book from the 25 bps repo hike and 10 bps passed on so far.
FY27 credit cost guidance of 10 bps maintained; gross NPA expected to fall in H2.
Plans to draw NHB refinance earlier, from Q3 if sanctions are higher, to benefit from lower rates; exploring an additional refinance limit.
capex_capacity: Project Tejas fully live: LOS and LMS live across all branches as of 1 October 2026; modules including risk, ALM, borrowings (by September 2025 onward) and deposits/DMS (January) implemented per management.

demand_pricing: Management said underlying demand is robust with no change, and attributed the Q2 shortfall to process changes (about 8-10 additional OTPs per borrower and co-borrower), a 5-day post-month data handover lag, and a new Telangana Section 22 sub-registrar verification requirement.
Housing loan rate raised by 10 bps effective 8 October 2026 (new customers from 12 October); about 87% of floating book is on quarterly reset, about 12-13% on annual reset.
Management expects a 25 bps repo hike to translate into about 12-13 bps on the book, with plans to pass on about 15 bps next time.

Prepayment rate was about 15.5-16% historically and about 17-17.5% recently; management said a 100 bps rise could narrow the rate gap by around 60 bps, reducing prepayment and rundown by about INR400 crore.
Higher-ticket (INR30 lakh+) loans have grown, and the company is also looking at AHF-linked INR15-25 lakh loans as NHB AHF share rises.
PMAY 2.0 uptake described as slow relative to CLSS-1, with limited presence in the high-need states (Odisha, Bengal, Bihar, UP).
Management said the sales team contributed INR560 crore in H1 FY27 and targets about 20% of disbursement from sales in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the liquidity coverage ratio rise well above the 100% regulatory minimum, and what is a steady level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to lower short-term borrowings, now about 12% of borrowings versus 26-27% in March 2023, plus smaller bulk borrowings. LCR range cited as 135% to 250%; HQLA held at roughly INR2,300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Does a rising rate cycle affect home loan demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 25-50 bps move is a non-event for demand because EMI impact is limited on 15-year tenors. Rates of 7.15-8% are among the lowest seen, so customer behaviour is not expected to change much.

qa_highlights.question: Is there risk to FY27 disbursement target from the South monsoon or drought, and to asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is early to assess; drought has been declared in parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka, but the company lends mainly in Tier 1-2 areas. If industry slows, it could hit disbursement, and it may use LAP or construction top-ups as short-term levers.

qa_highlights.question: How will operational efficiency from Project Tejas play out in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited manual processes now automated, native AI features, auto form filling, and a digital sourcing channel expected to reach about 10% of business. Sales headcount to rise from about 90 to 150 this year without adding branch staff.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rate pass-through and prepayment outlook after the repo hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Housing rates rose 10 bps effective 8 October 2026 against a 25 bps repo hike, which translates to about 12-13 bps on the book. Management said a 100 bps rise could cut the rate gap by about 60 bps and reduce prepayment and rundown by about INR400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How reset timing works for bank borrowings and the loan book, and whether spread is at risk in a rising cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Repo-linked bank borrowings reprice from 1 November; T-bill-linked ones reset quarterly. About 87% of the floating book is on quarterly reset and 12-13% on annual, with roughly one-third repricing each on 1 November, 1 December and 1 January. Management said it will pass on hikes to protect spread and NIM.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management in the H2 disbursement ramp (about INR3,500 crore per quarter) and the FY28 AUM outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was INR2,600 crore against a planned INR2,500 crore, so the INR100 crore buffer was used; Q3 target is INR3,500 crore with about INR400 crore shortfall recovered in Q4. FY28 disbursement target of INR16,000 crore implies AUM growth of about 15-15.5%, with 15% described as a resultant figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the productivity ramp for new branches and the pipeline status?
qa_highlights.answer: New branches take about 18 months (range 18-24) to reach 5 cases per staff per month. Management said sanctioned-but-not-disbursed rose about INR118 crore quarter on quarter, and that some pipeline was lost during the migration.

key_quotes: The month in which the implementation has happened, the disbursements, they have dropped in that particular branches by about 70% to 75%, and then the next month, again, it pushes back and it comes back to almost 80% -90% of the old disbursement.

Basically, in terms of the demand or in terms of the business per se, there has been no change, but for the impact of the IT transformation, which is mainly on account of the understanding, or rather the change in the flow, the additional processes that have been incorporated.
We will be looking at a 20% plus growth in terms of the disbursement, which consequently should become a 13%- 14% AUM growth this year and a 15% plus AUM growth in the next year.
Basically, our endeavor will be to ensure that our NIM and spread and NIM stays protected.

511218|2026-03.headline: Shriram Finance Q4 FY26 PAT rose 40.86% YoY to INR3,013.57 crores; management guides 18% AUM growth for FY27 but will revisit after Q1.
511218|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered strong profitability, with PAT up 40.86% YoY to INR3,013.57 crores and NIM up to 8.61%, while AUM grew 14.85% YoY to INR3,02,273.75 crores. Gross Stage 3 edged up to 4.58% from 4.55% a year ago, and Stage 2 plus Stage 3 rose sequentially in CV, PV and MSME. MUFG Bank completed a preferential allotment on April 8, 2026, taking a 20% fully diluted stake, and the board recommended a final dividend of INR6 per share. Management budgets 18% AUM growth and 8.5% NIM for FY27, but said Q1 FY27 is hard to predict and it will revisit guidance after Q1, with credit cost unchanged for now.

qa_highlights.question: Why did used PV financing slow in Q4, and what is the PV growth outlook?

511218|2026-06.headline: Shriram Finance Q1 FY27 PAT rose 59.79% YoY to INR3,444.56 crores, with NIM at 9.04% and disbursements up 19.51% YoY to INR49,974 crores.
511218|2026-06.overview: Shriram Finance reported strong Q1 FY27 numbers, with PAT of INR3,444.56 crores (up 59.79% YoY, up 14.3% QoQ) and NII up 33.67% YoY to INR8,055.70 crores. Growth was supported by fresh equity of about INR39,600 crores, which cut the leverage ratio to 2.14x from 3.82x in March and funded repayment of borrowings. Management reiterated the FY27 AUM growth guidance of 18% but said it will reassess after Q2, and guided credit cost around 2% and operational NIM around 8.5% in the medium term. Asset quality was broadly stable, with gross Stage 3 at 4.64% against 4.58% in Q4 FY26. Management said the company will now deploy surplus liquidity into growth and return to borrowing, including securitisation, towards the end of the quarter.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 CV disbursement INR19,556 crores, the largest product. Management said CV growth tracked the ~20% industry volume growth and new-vehicle share is rising.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 PV disbursement INR11,018 crores. Management cited industry PV sales growth of 25.9%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 MSME disbursement INR6,184 crores. Management targets MSME rising from about 15% to about 20% of the book, with growth expected to exceed the overall book.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 gold disbursement INR5,153 crores; gold is about 2.5% of the book, targeted at about 5% in three years, with about 2,200 branches gold-ready.

segments.name: Personal loans, 2-wheelers, construction and farm equipment
segments.commentary: Personal loans INR2,773 crores, 2-wheelers INR3,548 crores, construction equipment INR792 crores (about INR1,000 crores for five quarters), farm equipment INR947 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 18% is retained; management will reassess after Q2 FY27 and expects growth of more than 15% in Q2.
Operational NIM expected around 8.5% in the medium term (2-3 years); current NIM of about 9% expected to hold for the next two quarters as surplus liquidity is deployed.
Credit cost guided at around 2% in the near and medium term.
Cost-to-income ratio to remain stable; about 150 branches to be added in FY27 without a material rise in cost.
New vehicle share of disbursement (about 16-17%) expected to rise to about 20-25% over time, with new-vehicle book reaching about 30% plus of the book in the medium term.
Borrowing to resume around the end of Q2 (August to October), with securitisation likely; incremental borrowing cost about 7.77%, bank borrowing about 8%.
capex_capacity: About 150 new branches tentatively planned for FY27, with manpower to rise in line with volume.
About 2,200 branches made ready for gold loan activity; gold book targeted to double in three years.
Surplus liquidity of INR17,000-18,000 crores held as roughly three months of liability repayments; the balance of surplus is expected to be deployed into growth over about 1-1.5 months.
No liability repayments planned from here; borrowing programme to restart, with securitisation and direct assignment transactions not done in Q1.
demand_pricing: Industry: CV sales up 14.1% YoY to 2.65 lakh units; PV up 25.9%; 2-wheelers up 20.3%; 3-wheelers up 29.7%; tractors up 21.6%; construction equipment up 8.8%, per management.
Management said operators have absorbed fuel-cost increases without vehicle idling, and used-vehicle demand has stayed healthy.
Lower borrowing costs are being passed on to new-vehicle customers, and some customers who had left for other lenders are being won back by matching rates.
Management said the MSME slowdown in FY26 was due to US tariffs and policy uncertainty; the book is now expected to grow again from Q2.
Gold demand is driven by customers raising loans against existing jewellery, which management sees as a source of volume for NBFCs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the NIM hold at around 9%, given excess liquidity and a slow mix shift toward new vehicles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current NIM should hold for the next two quarters, but will fall to about 8.5% in the medium term as new-vehicle mix rises. Management said the INR500 crore of NII from equity-funded surplus liquidity will gradually subside.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 18% FY27 growth guidance be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management retained 18% for FY27, said it will reassess after Q2, and expects growth above 15% next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for asset quality in gold and MSME?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gold asset quality is not a concern, and MSME quality is improving after a cautious year. The Q1 Stage 3 rise was a seasonal impact, from 4.58% to 4.63%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of incremental borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bank borrowing would cost about 8%, and incremental capital-market borrowing about 7.77%; the company now borrows as a AA-rated entity, which lowers its cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why will the company borrow again if it holds surplus liquidity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the surplus will be used for growth over about 1-1.5 months, after which fresh borrowing will resume, including securitisation toward the end of the quarter.

risks_watch: Monsoon deficit: rainfall was 24% below normal from June 4 to July 16, and IMD forecasts 90% of normal rainfall for 2026, which could affect rural income and oilseed and pulse output.
West Asia conflict and fuel prices: management said pass-through has held so far, but a further rise in retail fuel prices could hit operator margins.
NIM trajectory: management guides NIM falling from 9.04% to about 8.5% in the medium term, and analysts questioned the pace.
MSME and gold: Stage 3 rose QoQ in gold and MSME; the MSME book must grow to about INR7,000 crores per quarter from Q3 to meet the target.
Borrowing restart: funding will move back toward market borrowings and securitisation after Q2, so the cost of funds and mix will be watched.
Construction equipment disbursement has stayed near INR1,000 crores for five quarters against about INR2,000 crores previously.
511218|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and asset quality, but cautious on the guidance path: management held the FY27 target, deferred any upgrade until after Q2, and repeatedly tied the outlook to monsoon and West Asia risk. Questions on the 8.5% medium-term NIM drew the most pushback from analysts.
key_quotes: But we are confident that we'll be able to grow more than 15% at least for next quarter.
So our long-term margins of 8.5%, we will be able to manage.
Gold, absolutely not. MSME, we have been cautious in the last 1 year. We are now pretty confident about the MSME quality -- asset quality.
Stable, I should say.

511218|2026-09.headline: Shriram Finance Q2 FY27 PAT rose 59.37% YoY to INR3,677.03 crores, with NIM at 9.52% and gross Stage 3 at 4.65%.
511218|2026-09.overview: Shriram Finance reported strong Q2 FY27 earnings, with disbursements up 25.71% YoY to INR54,079.02 crores and AUM up 16.96% YoY to INR3,29,021.72 crores. Net interest income rose to INR8,661.04 crores and NIM expanded to 9.52%, which management attributed partly to temporary capital-driven benefits. Asset quality weakened, with gross Stage 3 at 4.65% (4.64% in Q1) and credit cost at 2.03%, which management linked to weak monsoon and drought-prone geographies. Management trimmed AUM growth guidance to 15-17% from 18%, and said credit cost would be elevated by about 30-40 bps for one or two quarters.

financial_highlights.change: down 15 bps QoQ from 8.56%; down 18 bps since March

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Disbursements rose to roughly INR10,000 crores per the analyst's figure, versus about INR6,000 crores in recent quarters, as lending expanded from the South and West to all-India. Unsecured share is 28% and secured 72%; MSME is a source of incremental Stage 2 and Stage 3 accretion.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold disbursements were INR5,443 crores in Q2 versus INR5,153 crores in Q1. AUM is about INR9,000 crores, and LTV is about 72-73%. Management attributes higher gold Stage 2/3 to the newly introduced EMI and interest-servicing products, where customers are used to bullet repayment.

segments.name: Construction equipment
segments.commentary: Disbursements have rebounded, but Stage 2 and Stage 3 ratios rose. Management said absolute gross Stage 3 fell to INR862 crores from INR874 crores QoQ, and gross Stage 2 is INR963 crores versus INR953 crores, so the rise is a denominator effect.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: Liability mix is public deposits 31%, NCDs 15.71%, ECB and bonds 16.5%, bank and institutional borrowing 21%, and securitisation 14%, out of total liabilities of INR2,36,271 crores. Management said about INR27,000 crores was raised in the quarter, and liquidity was brought down to about 3 months of future liabilities.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth for FY27 is now expected at 15-17%, down from the earlier 18% guidance; Q1 growth was about 15% and Q2 about 17%.
Credit cost guidance is about 2% long term. Management said it may run 30-40 bps higher in select geographies and products for one or two quarters, and the full-year figure would be lower than 2.3%.
NIM is expected to stay near current levels for one or two quarters, then ease to around 9% in the medium term and about 8.5% in the long term.

Incremental cost of funds is expected to stay below 8%, potentially rising to about 8.35% if rates or capital market yields rise. Management does not expect the overall liability cost to rise from 8.4%.
Cost to income is guided to about 25% in the medium to long term, with technology spend likely to add to opex.
Gold loan target is unchanged: double the gold book in three years, from about 2.5% to about 5% of the book.

Insurance commission income of about INR350 crores in FY26 could fall by about INR100 crores if the draft IRDA distribution-income guidelines are adopted, which management called immaterial to the balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Liquidity has been drawn down to about 3 months of future liabilities, with cash plus investments falling from about INR38,000 crores to about INR31,000-32,000 crores. Future AUM growth will now largely need fresh borrowing rather than surplus liquidity.
Borrowing programme has resumed, with bonds and bank borrowing back to pre-March levels. Liquidity coverage ratio is 303%.
demand_pricing: Macro: Q1 FY27 GDP grew 7.8%, and the IMF raised its FY27 forecast to 7%. Retail CPI rose to 5.54% in September, and the RBI raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.5% with a calibrated tightening stance.

Rural and auto demand: the Q2 passenger vehicle sales growth was 30.7%, two-wheelers 15.2%, and commercial vehicles 28.7%. The monsoon was 87% of LPA, and 51.2% of India's area was abnormally dry or worse as of September 23.
Stress is concentrated in drought-prone states such as Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana. Management said it is cautious there but sees no widespread problem.
New versus used vehicle yield differential is 200-400 bps, depending on the segment.
Management said fresh loans can be repriced, but the existing fixed-rate book cannot be repriced.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the Stage 2 and Stage 3 increase across construction equipment, gold and MSME, and what credit cost is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonal weakness and certain geographies with lower rainfall, and said it is not widespread. Credit cost guidance stays at about 2%, with a possible 30 bps temporary increase in select areas. Loan-book Stage 3 is about 2.3%, not 2.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM and cost of funds evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM is elevated temporarily from capital infusion and will stay near current levels for one or two quarters, then ease to about 9% medium term and about 8.5% long term. Incremental cost of funds is expected below 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the AUM growth guidance lower, and are credit filters being tightened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is guided to 15-17% because of the West Asia war and weak monsoon, and said credit filters are unchanged unless the economy slows. Rural demand was strong in the last two quarters, and caution has only been applied to drought-prone areas in the last month.

qa_highlights.question: Are gold loan stress levels a sign of industry-level problems?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise is mainly from the new EMI and interest-servicing gold products, where customers used to bullet repayment are paying late, and it sees no industry-level challenge. The gold growth plan is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the draft IRDA distribution-income guidelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance commission was about INR350 crores in FY26, and the proposed guidelines could cut about INR100 crores. Management said this is not material to the balance sheet and expects IRDA to revise the rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why did opex growth stay benign, and what is the medium-term cost-to-income target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 included annual back-office bonuses, so Q2 staff costs normalised. The medium to long-term cost-to-income target is about 25%, with added technology spend as a risk.

risks_watch: Credit cost and Stage 3 could stay elevated for one or two quarters if the monsoon stays weak and in drought-prone areas such as Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana.
MSME is growing fast into new geographies and carries a high share of Stage 2 and Stage 3 accretion. Unsecured exposure is 28% of the MSME book.
Rising policy rates and capital market yields could push incremental borrowing costs above 8%, and the NIM could compress faster than the guided glide path.
Management did not quantify the share of slippages from drought-prone areas or the share of new vehicles in AUM, and it referred these to investor relations.
A reported unauthorised loan issue in Kerala was taken offline, with status and KYC controls not disclosed on the call.
Gold loan Stage 2 and Stage 3 are rising as customers move to EMI and interest-servicing products.

511243|2026-03.headline: Chola Q4 FY26 disbursements rose 25% YoY to INR32,913 crore, AUM up 21% to INR2,42,630 crore; FY27 credit cost guided to ~1.5% pre-overlay.

NIM rose 40 bps YoY to about 8% on lower cost of funds, and pre-overlay ROA was 4.1% versus 3.6% a year earlier. Management booked a INR200 crore precautionary management overlay for geopolitical and fuel-price risks, and said April 2026 early delinquencies, non-starters and first-cut net credit losses were better than April 2025. Guidance for FY27 is 20-23% AUM growth and net credit cost falling from 1.6% (pre-overlay) to about 1.5%.

segments.name: MSME (LAP, SME, SBPL)

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 AUM and credit cost trajectory, and what credit filter changes are being made?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth stays at 20-23% and net credit cost is expected to fall from 1.6% pre-overlay to about 1.5%, helped by Gini-coefficient improvements in underwriting. No further overlay is needed for now beyond the INR200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong April CV and PV data from OEMs reflected on the ground?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said April sales, credit and collections were very strong versus April 2025, and it has seen no change in customer behaviour.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CSEL growth, opex and ROA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CSEL pre-tax ROA is expected to exceed 3% this year from Q4 ROA of 2.3%. Q4 opex included a one-time CGTMSE cost (about 6% of the segment's opex), and the opex ratio should normalise to about 4.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the business loan book is covered by CGTMSE?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of unsecured assets are covered and this may rise to 80-82%. Only the business loan book is in CGTMSE, at about INR3,000-3,500 crore (about 80% of a roughly INR5,000 crore BL book); Q4 CGTMSE cost was about INR38 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Did the overlay change PD-LGD assumptions, and why is NIM up 50 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: No PD-LGD change was made; the overlay was set using COVID and diesel-price experience. The NIM jump relates to ARC receipts recognised as income, offset by higher credit losses, leaving ROTA largely unchanged.

511742|2026-03.headline: UGRO Capital says Q4 FY26 net total income rose 51% YoY to a figure not stated in the call, with GNPA at 2.5%, cost of borrowings at 10.16%, and FY27 opex guided to INR 490-500 crores.
511742|2026-03.overview: UGRO Capital's first full quarter of its February 2026 structural realignment saw AUM broadly flat QoQ as the non-focus intermediated (DSA-led Prime) book runs down and focus verticals (EM-LAP and embedded finance) grow; focus share rose from 33% to 38% of AUM. Net total income grew 51% YoY and 34% QoQ, and PAT grew 26% YoY, after a one-time restructuring cost of about INR 25 crores. Management reiterated five FY29 commitments (85% focus-vertical AUM, INR 220 crore cost takeout, 15-20% annual Prime run-down, no new equity, ROA of 3-3.5%), and said FY27 is a transition year with only marginal ROA improvement. Q&A focused on growth outlook, co-lending exit, embedded-finance credit quality and the Profectus acquisition economics. Note: the call's Q4 net total income level and total PAT were not stated in the transcript.

segments.commentary: Secured portfolio including machinery loans about 67% of total AUM with GNPA ~1.5%; unsecured (embedded plus business loans) capped at 30-35% of portfolio per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why exit the intermediated book, which was ~70% of AUM, and why stop co-lending?

Secured EM-LAP has credit cost in the same band despite higher GNPA.

qa_highlights.question: Will AUM grow? Growth is slowing.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire Profectus given the planned shift to higher yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Profectus (INR ~180 crore cost base) was used to rationalise opex; the acquired portfolio generates cash profit that supports the new branch network, and the deal is ROE-accretive by ~10%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said total outstanding shares are 15.29 crore on a fully diluted basis, with 2 lakh shares pending conversion; all CCDs and warrants are matured or converted.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ARC transaction details and how do they compare with prior ARC deals?

qa_highlights.question: What is the accounting impact of the ARC sale on profit?

511766|2026-09.headline: Muthoot Capital Q2 FY27 PAT of Rs 4.11 crore, AUM Rs 3,530 crore (+25% YoY), GNPA up to 4.61% with forward flow down to 0.50%.
511766|2026-09.overview: Management described H1 FY27 as a consolidation period, highlighted the Brickwork upgrade to AA, and reported AUM of Rs 3,530 crore, up 25% YoY, with Q2 fresh disbursements of Rs 677 crore. Co-lending was run down to Rs 382 crore from Rs 791 crore a year earlier, lifting the blended yield, while borrowing costs fell by 0.61% for bank loans. Asset quality was mixed: GNPA rose to 4.61% from 5.76% a year ago (and was higher QoQ), but forward flow to NPA fell to 0.50% and impairment was Rs 21.44 crore in the quarter. Management reiterated a ~4% ROA goal, with CV and used car still in investment phase.

segments.commentary: Combined book of about Rs 350-356 crore with GNPA near 0.35%; disbursements rose over 100% in H1, with breakeven targeted by end of FY27.

segments.commentary: Rs 422 crore of AUM with 5.70% GNPA, a key driver of the elevated asset quality ratio.

guidance_outlook: AUM exit FY27 closer to Rs 4,200 crore.

Disbursements expected at Rs 400+ crore per month in November onward, after Rs 306 crore in October (highest ever October).

Two-wheeler yield on MCSL's own book is 21.5-22%; the blended yield rose as lower-yielding co-lending shrank.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving retail book growth and what is the FY27 target?
